en: Then, indeed, this thought occurred to those sons of the gods:
"What kind of persons should be sought as listeners to the Dharma from the Elder Subhūti?
Then the Venerable Subhūti, knowing with his own mind the reflection in the minds of those sons of the gods, addressed those sons of the gods as follows:
"O sons of the gods, my teaching of the Dharma should be regarded by me as like an illusion; O sons of the gods, those who hear the Dharma should be regarded by me as like an illusion.
O sons of the gods, my teaching of the Dharma should be regarded by me as like a magical creation; O sons of the gods, those who hear the Dharma should be regarded by me as like a magical creation.
They shall hear nothing at all, nor shall they realize anything."
Then the sons of the gods said this to the venerable Subhūti:

"But, Venerable Subhūti, are those beings like an illusion, and are those listeners of the Dharma like an illusion? Are those beings like a magical creation, and are those listeners of the Dharma like a magical creation?"
Subhūti said: "So it is, sons of gods; so it is.
Those beings are like an illusion, and those who listen to the Dharma are like an illusion."
Those beings are like magical emanations; those listeners of the Dharma are like magical emanations. Those sons of the gods, those beings, are like dreams;
those sons of the gods, those beings, are like illusions.
Form, too, O sons of the gods, is like a dream and like an illusion.

O sons of the gods, feeling also is like a dream, like an illusion; perception also, O sons of the gods, is like a dream, like an illusion; mental formations also, O sons of the gods, are like a dream, like an illusion.
O sons of the gods, consciousness also is like a dream, like an illusion.
The eye also is like a dream, like an illusion; the ear also is like a dream, like an illusion.
The nose, too, is like a dream, like an illusion; the tongue, too, is like a dream, like an illusion;
the body, too, is like a dream, like an illusion.
The mind, too, is like a dream, like an illusion;
form, too, is like a dream, like an illusion;
sound, too, is like a dream, like an illusion.
Odor, too, is like a dream, like an illusion; taste, too, is like a dream, like an illusion; touch, too, is like a dream, like an illusion.
Phenomena, too, are like a dream, like an illusion;
visual consciousness, too, is like a dream, like an illusion; auditory consciousness, too, is like a dream, like an illusion.
It is like a dream, like an illusion;
olfactory consciousness also is like a dream, like an illusion;
gustatory consciousness also is like a dream, like an illusion.
Body-consciousness also is like a dream, like an illusion;
mind-consciousness also is like a dream, like an illusion.
Eye-contact also is like a dream, like an illusion.
Auditory contact, too, is like a dream, like an illusion;
olfactory contact, too, is like a dream, like an illusion;
gustatory contact, too, is like a dream, like an illusion.
Body-contact as well is like a dream, like an illusion; mind-contact as well is like a dream, like an illusion.
Even feeling born of eye-contact is like a dream, like an illusion.
Feeling born of ear-contact is also like a dream, like an illusion; feeling born of nose-contact is also like a dream, like an illusion;
feeling born of tongue-contact is also like a dream, like an illusion.
Feeling born of body-contact is like a dream, like an illusion;
feeling born of mind-contact is also like a dream, like an illusion. Even the earth element is like a dream, like an illusion.
The water element is like a dream, like an illusion; the fire element is like a dream, like an illusion;
the wind element is like a dream, like an illusion.
The space element is also like a dream, like an illusion;
the consciousness element is also like a dream, like an illusion.
Ignorance, too, is like a dream, like an illusion.
Formations also are like a dream, like an illusion;
consciousness also is like a dream, like an illusion;
name-and-form also is like a dream, like an illusion.
The six sense bases are also like a dream, like an illusion; contact too is like a dream, like an illusion; feeling too is like a dream, like an illusion.
Craving, too, is like a dream and like an illusion;
grasping, too, is like a dream and like an illusion;
existence, too, is like a dream and like an illusion.
Birth, too, is like a dream, like an illusion;
old age and death, too, are like a dream, like an illusion.
Even the perfection of generosity is like a dream, like an illusion.
The perfection of ethical discipline is like a dream, like an illusion; the perfection of patience is like a dream, like an illusion;
the perfection of vigor is also like a dream, like an illusion.
The perfection of meditation is also like a dream, like an illusion;
the perfection of wisdom is also like a dream, like an illusion.
Even internal emptiness is like a dream, like an illusion.
External emptiness also is like a dream, like an illusion;
internal-external emptiness also is like a dream, like an illusion;
the emptiness of emptiness also is like a dream, like an illusion.
Great emptiness, too, is like a dream, like an illusion; ultimate emptiness, too, is like a dream, like an illusion;
conditioned emptiness, too, is like a dream, like an illusion.
Unconditioned emptiness is like a dream, like an illusion;
absolute emptiness is like a dream, like an illusion;
emptiness without beginning or end is also like a dream, like an illusion.
Non-dispersal emptiness is like a dream, like an illusion; intrinsic nature emptiness is like a dream, like an illusion;
the emptiness of all phenomena is also like a dream, like an illusion.
The emptiness of specific characteristics is like a dream and like an illusion;
the emptiness of non-apprehension is also like a dream and like an illusion; the emptiness of non-existence is also like a dream and like an illusion.
Even the emptiness of intrinsic nature is like a dream, like an illusion;
even the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence is like a dream, like an illusion.
Even the applications of mindfulness are like dreams, like illusions.
The right efforts are also like dreams and like illusions;
the bases of psychic power are also like dreams and like illusions;
the faculties are also like dreams and like illusions.
The powers, too, are like a dream, like an illusion;
the factors of enlightenment, too, are like a dream, like an illusion;
even the noble eightfold path is like a dream, like an illusion.
The noble truths, too, are like a dream, like an illusion;
the meditative concentrations, too, are like a dream, like an illusion;
the immeasurables, too, are like a dream, like an illusion.
The formless attainments are also like a dream, like an illusion; the liberations are also like a dream, like an illusion;
the serial attainments are also like a dream, like an illusion.
The gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—are like dreams and like illusions;
the superknowledges are also like dreams and like illusions;
even the meditative concentrations are like dreams and like illusions.
The gateways of dhāraṇī are also like a dream, like an illusion;
the powers of a Tathāgata are also like a dream, like an illusion;
the grounds of self-confidence are also like a dream, like an illusion.
The analytical knowledges (pratisaṃvid) are also like a dream, like an illusion;
great loving-kindness (mahāmaitrī) is also like a dream, like an illusion; great compassion (mahākaruṇā) is also like a dream, like an illusion.
The unique attributes of a Buddha are also like a dream, like an illusion.
The fruit of stream-entry is also like a dream, like an illusion; the fruit of once-returning is also like a dream, like an illusion.
The fruit of non-returning is also like a dream, like an illusion;
arhatship is also like a dream, like an illusion;
even the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha is like a dream, like an illusion.
"Even perfect enlightenment is like a dream, like an illusion.
Then those sons of the gods said this to the venerable Subhūti:
"Subhūti, you say that even enlightenment is like a dream, like an illusion. Why then do you say that even nirvāṇa is like a dream, like an illusion?"
Subhūti said:
"O sons of the gods, I declare even nirvāṇa to be like a dream and like an illusion; were there any other dharma more distinguished than that nirvāṇa,"
I would say that even this is like a dream and like an illusion. For what reason?
Because, O sons of the gods, a dream, an illusion, and nirvāṇa—these are non-dual and cannot be divided.
Then the venerable Śāradvatīputra and the venerable Mahāmaudgalyāyana...
The Venerable Mahākauṣṭhilya, the Venerable Mahākātyāyana, and the Venerable Pūrṇamaitrāyaṇīputra.
The venerable Mahākāśyapa and many thousands of bodhisattvas said this to the venerable Subhūti:

"Venerable Subhūti, who is it that can [fully comprehend] this profound perfection of wisdom, which is thus difficult to see, thus difficult to realize, thus peaceful, thus subtle, thus refined, and thus excellent?
Then the venerable Subhūti spoke thus to those great śrāvakas and those bodhisattva mahāsattvas:

Venerable ones, irreversible bodhisattva mahāsattvas are those who accept this very Prajñāpāramitā— so profound, so beyond ratiocination, so outside the sphere of ratiocination, so subtle, so precise, so difficult to see, so difficult to understand, so peaceful, so sublime, so perfectly noble, and so to be realized by the wise and the learned.

Or those persons who have seen the truths, or Arhats whose outflows are exhausted and whose intentions are fulfilled; those beings who have performed services for previous Victors and planted roots of merit under many millions of Buddhas; and those sons of good family and daughters of good family who are sustained by spiritual friends—[all these] regarding this very profound perfection of wisdom, which is thus beyond reasoning and beyond the sphere of reasoning.

When this which is so subtle, so refined, so difficult to see, so difficult to understand, so peaceful, so sublime, so sufficient for the noble ones, and so to be realized by the wise and learned is being taught, there will be those who accept it. Furthermore, they will not conceptualize that "form is empty."
They will not conceptualize form as emptiness,
nor will they conceptualize feeling as empty,
nor will they conceptualize emptiness as feeling.

They will not conceptualize that "formative forces are peaceful," nor will they conceptualize that "consciousness is peaceful," nor will they conceptualize that "consciousness is peaceful."

They will not conceptualize non-arising as the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha; they will not conceptualize the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha as non-cessation; they will not conceptualize non-cessation as the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.
They will not conceptualize the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha as "peaceful," nor will they conceptualize the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha as "peace";
they will not conceptualize the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha as "secluded."
They will not conceptualize that the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are secluded.
They will not conceptualize that the fruit of stream-entry is empty,
nor will they conceptualize that emptiness is the fruit of stream-entry.
They will not conceptualize that the fruit of stream-entry is signless, nor will they conceptualize that the signless is the fruit of stream-entry;
they will not conceptualize that the fruit of stream-entry is wishless.
They will not conceptualize that the fruit of stream-entry is wishless;
they will not conceptualize that the fruit of stream-entry is non-arising;
they will not conceptualize that non-arising is the fruit of stream-entry.

They will not conceptualize that the fruit of stream-entry is non-extinction, nor will they conceptualize that non-extinction is the fruit of stream-entry, nor will they conceptualize that the fruit of stream-entry is peace.
They will not conceptualize that the fruit of stream-entry is peaceful;
they will not conceptualize that the fruit of stream-entry is secluded;
they will not conceptualize that the fruit of stream-entry is secluded.
They will not conceptualize that the fruit of once-returning is empty;
they will not conceptualize that emptiness is the fruit of once-returning;
they will not conceptualize that the fruit of once-returning is signless.
They will not conceptualize that the fruit of once-returning is signless;
they will not conceptualize that the fruit of once-returning is wishless;
they will not conceptualize that the wishless is the fruit of once-returning.
They will not conceptualize the fruit of once-returning as non-arising;
they will not conceptualize non-arising as the fruit of once-returning; they will not conceptualize the fruit of once-returning as non-cessation.
They will not conceptualize that the fruit of once-returning is non-cessation;
they will not conceptualize that the fruit of once-returning is peace; nor will they conceptualize that the fruit of once-returning is peaceful.
They will not conceptualize that the fruit of once-returning is secluded,
nor will they conceptualize that the fruit of once-returning is secluded; they will not conceptualize that the fruit of non-returning is empty.
They will not conceptualize emptiness as the fruit of non-returning; they will not conceptualize the fruit of non-returning as signlessness;
they will not conceptualize signlessness as the fruit of non-returning.

They will conceptualize that the fruit of the non-returner is wishlessness; they will conceptualize that wishlessness is the fruit of the non-returner; they will conceptualize that the fruit of the non-returner is non-arising.

They will not conceptualize non-arising as the fruit of non-returning; they will not conceptualize the fruit of non-returning as non-cessation; they will not conceptualize non-cessation as the fruit of non-returning.
They will not conceptualize that the fruit of the non-returner is peaceful,
nor will they conceptualize that the fruit of the non-returner is not peaceful; they will not conceptualize that the fruit of the non-returner is secluded.
They will not conceptualize that the fruit of non-returning is secluded; they will not conceptualize that arhatship is empty;
nor will they conceptualize that emptiness is arhatship.
They will not conceptualize that "arhatship is signless," nor will they conceptualize that "the signless is arhatship," nor will they conceptualize that "arhatship is wishless."
They will not conceptualize that "arhatship is wishless," nor will they conceptualize that "arhatship is non-arising," nor will they conceptualize that "non-arising is arhatship."
They will not conceptualize that "arhatship is non-ceasing," nor will they conceptualize that "non-ceasing is arhatship," nor will they conceptualize that "arhatship is peaceful."
They will not conceptualize that arhatship is peaceful;
they will not conceptualize that arhatship is secluded; they will not conceptualize that arhatship is seclusion.
They will not conceptualize solitary enlightenment as empty; they will not conceptualize emptiness as solitary enlightenment;
they will not conceptualize solitary enlightenment as signless.

They will not conceptualize that "the signless is solitary awakening," nor will they conceptualize that "solitary awakening is the wishless," nor will they conceptualize that "the wishless is solitary awakening."
They will not conceptualize that individual enlightenment is non-arising,
nor will they conceptualize that non-arising is individual enlightenment; they will not conceptualize that individual enlightenment is non-cessation.
They will not conceptualize that "pratyekabodhi is non-cessation," nor will they conceptualize that "pratyekabodhi is peace," nor will they conceptualize that "peace is pratyekabodhi."
They will not conceptualize solitary awakening as "secluded," nor will they conceptualize solitude as "solitary awakening";
they will not conceptualize the knowledge of the aspects of the path as "empty."

They will not conceptualize emptiness as the knowledge of the aspects of the path; they will not conceptualize the knowledge of the aspects of the path as signlessness; they will not conceptualize signlessness as the knowledge of the aspects of the path.
They will not conceptualize the knowledge of the aspects of the path as being wishless, nor will they conceptualize the wishless as being the knowledge of the aspects of the path;
they will not conceptualize the knowledge of the aspects of the path as being non-arising.

They will not conceptualize non-arising as the knowledge of the aspects of the path; they will not conceptualize the knowledge of the aspects of the path as non-cessation; they will not conceptualize non-cessation as the knowledge of the aspects of the path.
They will not conceptualize the knowledge of the aspects of the path as "peaceful," nor will they conceptualize peacefulness as the knowledge of the aspects of the path;
they will not conceptualize the knowledge of the aspects of the path as "secluded."
They will not conceptualize that the knowledge of the aspects of the path is secluded;
they will not conceptualize that the knowledge of all aspects is empty; nor will they conceptualize that emptiness is the knowledge of all aspects.
They will not conceptualize that the knowledge of all aspects is signless, nor will they conceptualize that the signless is the knowledge of all aspects;
they will not conceptualize that the knowledge of all aspects is wishless.
They will not conceptualize that the wishless is omniscience;
they will not conceptualize that omniscience is non-arising;
they will not conceptualize that non-arising is omniscience.
They will not conceptualize that omniscience is non-cessation,
nor will they conceptualize that non-cessation is omniscience;
they will not conceptualize that omniscience is peace.

They will not conceptualize that "all-aspect omniscience is peaceful," nor will they conceptualize that "all-aspect omniscience is secluded," nor will they conceptualize that "the secluded is all-aspect omniscience."
They will not conceptualize the conditioned realm as empty;
they will not conceptualize emptiness as the conditioned realm;
they will not conceptualize the conditioned realm as signless.
They will not conceptualize the signless as the conditioned realm;
they will not conceptualize the conditioned realm as the wishless; nor will they conceptualize the wishless as the conditioned realm.
They will not conceptualize the conditioned realm as non-arising,
nor will they conceptualize non-arising as the conditioned realm; they will not conceptualize the conditioned realm as non-cessation.
They will not conceptualize that the conditioned realm is non-ceasing;
they will not conceptualize that the conditioned realm is peaceful;
nor will they conceptualize that peace is the conditioned realm.
They will not conceptualize the conditioned realm as "secluded," nor will they conceptualize the secluded as the "conditioned realm";
they will not conceptualize the unconditioned realm as "empty."
They will not conceptualize emptiness as the unconditioned realm;
they will not conceptualize the unconditioned realm as signlessness;
nor will they conceptualize signlessness as the unconditioned realm.
They will not conceptualize the unconditioned realm as being wishless,
nor will they conceptualize the wishless as being the unconditioned realm; nor will they conceptualize the unconditioned realm as being non-arising.
They will not conceptualize non-arising as the unconditioned realm; they will not conceptualize the unconditioned realm as non-cessation;
they will not conceptualize non-cessation as the unconditioned realm.
They will not conceptualize the unconditioned realm as "peaceful," nor will they conceptualize the unconditioned realm as "peace";
they will not conceptualize the unconditioned realm as "secluded."
They will not conceptualize that the unconditioned realm (*asaṃskṛtadhātu*) is secluded.

By this method, O sons of the gods, [they will understand] this profound perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*), which is thus profound, thus beyond reasoning, thus outside the sphere of reasoning, thus subtle, thus exquisite, thus difficult to see, thus difficult to realize, and thus peaceful.
For such a well-expounded, thus sufficient, noble, and thus to be experienced by the wise and learned, there will be no one at all who accepts it. Why is that?
Because herein no dharma whatsoever is indicated nor illuminated. Just as herein no dharma whatsoever is indicated nor illuminated, even so herein no sentient being whatsoever exists.
Then the Venerable Śāradvatīputra said this to the Venerable Subhūti:

"But, Venerable Subhūti, here in this perfection of wisdom, the three vehicles—the vehicle of the śrāvaka, the vehicle of the pratyekabuddha, and the vehicle of the perfectly enlightened buddha—are not established in detail. Nor is the complete support of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, taught; nor is the path of the bodhisattvas taught, from the first production of the thought of awakening up to the tenth production of the thought of awakening."

and the perfection of patience.

and the playful displays of the superknowledges of the Bodhisattvas, the Mahāsattvas, are taught. In this way, indeed, the Bodhisattvas...
Great beings practicing the perfection of wisdom will be of miraculous birth. Likewise, they will possess the superknowledges and be of a nature not subject to decline;
they will travel from buddhafield to buddhafield, and with whatever roots of merit they may desire, they will honor, revere, and respect those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones.
In order to worship them, those roots of merit will flourish accordingly; and whatever Dharma they shall hear from those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones,
that shall never be interrupted.
Until they attain the knowledge of all modes, they will always be in a state of meditative equipoise,
undistracted by virtue of their yoga of equipoise;
and they will possess unimpeded eloquence.
They will possess unassailable eloquence;
they will possess coherent eloquence,
and they will possess lucid eloquence.
They will possess eloquence that is coherent,

Subhūti said: "So it is, venerable Śāradvatīputra; so it is.
It is exactly as you have said: here in this Perfection of Wisdom, the three vehicles have been taught in detail—the vehicle of the śrāvakas..."
The vehicle of the pratyekabuddhas and the vehicle of the perfectly awakened ones have been taught for the sake of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas;

The eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha and the playful exercises of the superknowledges of a bodhisattva mahāsattva are taught. Indeed, it is in this way that bodhisattva mahāsattvas, while practicing the perfection of wisdom, will be born by apparitional birth; thus they become those whose nature is not to fall away from the superknowledges.
They will travel from buddha-field to buddha-field,
and whatever roots of merit they may desire, those very roots of merit will be fulfilled so that they may honor, revere, respect, and worship those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones;
and they shall hear the Dharma from the presence of those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones.

They shall never be interrupted until they attain all-aspect omniscience (*sarvākārajñatā*). and they will possess a distinguished eloquence that transcends all the world.

'For what reason, venerable Subhūti, are the three vehicles taught in detail here in this perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*)?'"

The playful mastery of the superknowledges (*abhijñāvikrīḍita*) of the bodhisattva mahāsattva is taught. It is said that bodhisattva mahāsattvas practicing in this way within the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*) will be of spontaneous birth (*upapāduka*); likewise, they will possess the quality of non-retrogression regarding the superknowledges.
They will travel from buddha-field to buddha-field,
and by whatever roots of merit they may desire, they will acquire such roots of merit as are necessary to honor, revere, respect, and worship those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones;
and they will hear the Dharma from the presence of those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones.

They shall never be interrupted until they attain all-aspect omniscience (*sarvākārajñatā*). They shall always be in a state of meditative equipoise through the yoga of undistracted concentration. They shall possess unimpeded eloquence (*asaṅgapratibhāna*) and unbreakable eloquence; they shall possess eloquence born of meditative equipoise.
They will possess appropriate eloquence,
they will possess coherent eloquence,
and they will possess meaningful eloquence.
"And those bodhisattva mahāsattvas will possess a distinguished eloquence that transcends all worlds, by means of the yoga of non-apprehension.

And by whatever roots of merit they may desire to honor, revere, respect, and worship those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, such roots of merit as are required will be fully accomplished for them; and they shall hear the Dharma from the presence of those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones.

They shall never be interrupted until they attain the knowledge of all modes (*sarvākārajñatā*). They will possess appropriate eloquence,
they will possess coherent eloquence,
and they will possess meaningful eloquence.
And by means of the yoga of non-apprehension, these bodhisattva mahāsattvas will possess a distinguished eloquence that transcends all worlds.

Then, it occurred to Śakra, the lord of the gods: "While this rain of all dharmas is being spoken by the elder Subhūti, what if I were to magically create flowers and offer them to the Buddha, the Blessed One, the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, the community of monks, and the elder Subhūti?"
For the purpose of making an offering to this Perfection of Wisdom, I would scatter, shower down, and strew [flowers],

as many as there are gods of the Four Great Kings, the Trāyastriṃśa gods, the Yāma gods, the Tuṣita gods, the Nirmāṇarati gods, the Paranirmitavaśavartin gods, and the Brahmakāyika gods within the triple-thousand great thousandfold world system.

The gods who are the Ministers of Brahmā, the gods who are the Retinue of Brahmā, the gods who are the Great Brahmās, the gods of Radiance, the gods of Limited Radiance, the gods of Immeasurable Radiance, the gods of Utmost Radiance, the gods of Purity, the gods of Limited Purity, the gods of Immeasurable Purity,
the gods of Universal Purity, the gods of Vastness, the gods of Limited Vastness, the gods of Immeasurable Vastness, and the gods of Vast Fruit.
The Abṛha gods, the Atapa gods, the Sudṛśa gods, the Sudarśana gods, and the Akaniṣṭha gods had this thought:
"While this rain of Dharma is being spoken by the Elder Subhūti, what if we were now to conjure forth flowers and scatter them over the Buddha,
the Blessed One, the Bodhisattvas, the community of monks, and the Elder Subhūti, for the sake of this Perfection of Wisdom?"
"I shall scatter these for the purpose of worship.

Then indeed Śakra, the lord of the gods, [summoned] those gods belonging to the assembly of the Four Great Kings, the Trāyastriṃśa gods, the Yāma gods, the Tuṣita gods, the Nirmāṇarati gods, and the Paranirmitavaśavartin gods within this trichiliocosm.
the gods of the Brahma-realm, the gods who are ministers of Brahmā, the gods who are the retinue of Brahmā, the gods of Great Brahmā, the gods of Radiance,
the gods of Limited Radiance, the gods of Immeasurable Radiance, the gods of Streaming Radiance, the gods of Purity, the gods of Limited Purity,
the gods of Immeasurable Purity, the gods of Universal Purity, the gods of Vastness, the gods of Limited Vastness, and the gods of Immeasurable Vastness.

The Bṛhatphala gods, the Abṛha gods, the Atapa gods, the Sudṛśa gods, the Sudarśana gods, and the Akaniṣṭha gods— all of them, having miraculously created divine Māndārava flowers, scattered them over the Buddha, the Blessed One, the Bodhisattvas,
the Mahāsattvas, the community of monks, and the Elder Subhūti, as an act of worship for this Perfection of Wisdom.
They scattered them and strewed them,
with those flowers of great color.

This great trichiliocosm world-system became strewn with a carpet of flowers, and above in the sky, a flower-pavilion identical in size to the great trichiliocosm world-system was established, beautiful and delightful; then, Subhūti the Elder thought to himself:
Moreover, these flowers, which are being showered down, have never before been seen by me even in all the abodes of the gods;
these flowers that have been scattered by the gods are indeed created by them.

These flowers which have been scattered by the sons of the gods are not produced from stalks, nor are they land-born, nor are they water-born; these flowers are mind-made, for these flowers scattered by the sons of the gods are not produced from stalks.
Then Śakra, the lord of the gods, having understood with his own mind the reflection in the mind of the elder Subhūti, said this to the venerable elder Subhūti:
"Venerable Subhūti, these flowers have not issued forth; they are not made of mind, nor have they issued from a stalk."
Subhūti said:
"Furthermore, Kauśika, as for what you say: 'These flowers have not come forth; these flowers have not come forth from the mind, nor have they come forth from a trunk.'"
"Kauśika, those flowers which have not issued forth—these are not flowers.
Śakra said: "But, Reverend Subhūti, are only these flowers not issued forth?"
Furthermore, form also is unemerged; likewise, feeling is unemerged, perception is unemerged, mental formations are unemerged, and consciousness also is unemerged.
Subhūti said:
"O Kauśika, as for what you have said thus..."
“Kauśika, it is not only these flowers that are unproduced;
form (rūpa) also, Kauśika, is unproduced. And that which is unproduced is not form. Feeling (vedanā) also, Kauśika, is unproduced; and that which is unproduced is not feeling.”
Perception also, Kauśika, is unproduced; that which is unproduced is not perception.
Volitional formations also, Kauśika, are unproduced; those which are unproduced are not volitional formations.
Consciousness also, Kauśika, is unproduced; that which is unproduced is not consciousness.
The eye, Kauśika, is non-issuing; and that which is non-issuing is not the eye. The ear, Kauśika, is non-issuing; and that which is non-issuing is not the ear.
The nose, Kauśika, is non-issuing; and that which is non-issuing is not the nose.
The tongue, Kauśika, is non-emergent; that which is non-emergent is not the tongue. The body, Kauśika, is non-emergent; that which is non-emergent is not the body.
The mind, Kauśika, is non-emergent; that which is non-emergent is not the mind.

O Kauśika, form is non-emergent; that which is non-emergent is not form. Sound, O Kauśika, is non-emergent; that which is non-emergent is not sound. Odor, O Kauśika, is non-emergent; that which is non-emergent is not odor.
O Kauśika, taste is unproduced; that which is unproduced is not taste. Touch is unproduced; that which is unproduced is not touch.
Phenomena are unproduced; those which are unproduced are not phenomena.

Eye-consciousness, Kauśika, is non-emergent; and that which is non-emergent is not eye-consciousness. Ear-consciousness, Kauśika, is non-emergent; and that which is non-emergent is not ear-consciousness. Nose-consciousness, Kauśika, is non-emergent; and that which is non-emergent is not nose-consciousness.
Tongue-consciousness, Kauśika, is non-emergent; and that which is non-emergent is not tongue-consciousness.
Body-consciousness, Kauśika, is non-emergent; and that which is non-emergent is not body-consciousness.
Mental consciousness, Kauśika, is non-emergent; and that which is non-emergent is not mental consciousness.
Eye-contact, Kauśika, is unproduced; and that which is unproduced is not eye-contact. Ear-contact, Kauśika, is unproduced; and that which is unproduced is not ear-contact.
Nose-contact, Kauśika, is unproduced; and that which is unproduced is not nose-contact.
Tongue-contact, Kauśika, is non-emergent; that which is non-emergent is not tongue-contact. Body-contact, Kauśika, is non-emergent; that which is non-emergent is not body-contact.
Mind-contact, Kauśika, is non-emergent; that which is non-emergent is not mind-contact.
Kauśika, feeling conditioned by eye-contact is unproduced; that which is unproduced is not feeling conditioned by eye-contact.

Feeling conditioned by ear-contact, Kauśika, is unproduced; that which is unproduced is not feeling conditioned by ear-contact. Feeling conditioned by nose-contact, Kauśika, is unproduced; that which is unproduced is not feeling conditioned by nose-contact.

Feeling conditioned by tongue-contact, Kauśika, is unproduced; and that which is unproduced is not feeling conditioned by tongue-contact. Feeling conditioned by body-contact, Kauśika, is unproduced; and that which is unproduced is not feeling conditioned by body-contact.
Feeling conditioned by mind-contact, Kauśika, is unproduced; and that which is unproduced is not feeling conditioned by mind-contact.
The earth element, Kauśika, is non-emergent; that which is non-emergent is not the earth element.

Ignorance, Kauśika, is unproduced; that which is unproduced is not ignorance. Formations, Kauśika, are unproduced; those which are unproduced are not formations. Consciousness, Kauśika, is unproduced; that which is unproduced is not consciousness.
Kauśika, name-and-form is non-emergent; that which is non-emergent is not name-and-form.
The six sense bases, Kauśika, are non-emergent; that which is non-emergent is not the six sense bases. Contact, Kauśika, is non-emergent; that which is non-emergent is not contact.
Feeling, Kauśika, is unproduced; that which is unproduced is not feeling.
Craving, Kauśika, is unproduced; that which is unproduced is not craving. Grasping, Kauśika, is unproduced; that which is unproduced is not grasping.
Existence, Kauśika, is unproduced; and that which is unproduced is not existence. Birth, Kauśika, is unproduced; and that which is unproduced is not birth.
Old age and death, Kauśika, are unproduced; and that which is unproduced is not old age and death.

Kauśika, the perfection of giving is not produced; that which is not produced is not the perfection of giving. Kauśika, the perfection of ethical discipline is not produced; that which is not produced is not the perfection of ethical discipline.

The perfection of patience, Kauśika, is not produced; that which is not produced is not the perfection of patience. The perfection of vigor, Kauśika, is not produced; that which is not produced is not the perfection of vigor.
The perfection of meditation, Kauśika, is not produced; that which is not produced is not the perfection of meditation.

Kauśika, the perfection of wisdom is not produced; and that which is not produced is not the perfection of wisdom. Inner emptiness, Kauśika, is not produced; and that which is not produced is not inner emptiness.
Outer emptiness, Kauśika, is not produced; and that which is not produced is not outer emptiness.

Kauśika, internal-external emptiness is non-emergent; that which is non-emergent is not internal-external emptiness. Kauśika, the emptiness of emptiness is non-emergent; that which is non-emergent is not the emptiness of emptiness.
Kauśika, great emptiness is non-emergent; that which is non-emergent is not great emptiness.
The emptiness of the ultimate, Kauśika, is not produced; that which is not produced is not the emptiness of the ultimate.
The emptiness of the conditioned, Kauśika, is not produced; that which is not produced is not the emptiness of the conditioned.
The emptiness of the unconditioned, Kauśika, is not produced; that which is not produced is not the emptiness of the unconditioned.
The absolute emptiness, Kauśika, is non-issuing; that which is non-issuing is not absolute emptiness.
The emptiness without beginning or end, Kauśika, is non-issuing; that which is non-issuing is not the emptiness without beginning or end.
The emptiness of non-dispersal, Kauśika, is non-issuing; that which is non-issuing is not the emptiness of non-dispersal.

The emptiness of non-apprehension, Kauśika, is not produced; and that which is not produced is not the emptiness of non-apprehension. The emptiness of non-existence, Kauśika, is not produced; and that which is not produced is not the emptiness of non-existence.
The emptiness of intrinsic nature, Kauśika, is not produced; and that which is not produced is not the emptiness of intrinsic nature.

The faculties, Kauśika, are not produced; those which are not produced are not the faculties. The powers, Kauśika, are not produced; those which are not produced are not the powers.

Kauśika, those superknowledges which have not emerged, and those which have not emerged, are not superknowledges.

Kauśika, those gateways of dhāraṇī which have not emerged and those which have not emerged are not those gateways of dhāraṇī;

The four analytical knowledges, Kauśika, are not produced; that which is not produced is not those analytical knowledges. Great loving-kindness, Kauśika, is not produced; that which is not produced is not great loving-kindness.

Kauśika, one who has not set out is not a non-returner; and he who has not set out is not a non-returner. Kauśika, one who has not set out is not an arhat; and he who has not set out is not an arhat.
Kauśika, a pratyekabuddha is not one who has gone forth; and he who has not gone forth is not a pratyekabuddha.
Kauśika, a bodhisattva is not one who has gone forth; and he who has not gone forth is not a bodhisattva.
Kauśika, a tathāgata is not one who has gone forth; and he who has not gone forth is not a tathāgata.
Then it occurred to Śakra, the lord of the gods:
"How profound is the wisdom of this Elder Subhūti! For he neither contradicts conventional designation nor fails to teach the true nature of phenomena.
Then the Blessed One addressed Śakra, the lord of the gods:
"So it is, Kauśika, so it is! Deep indeed is the wisdom of this Elder Subhūti, in that he does not contradict conventional designation while yet teaching the true nature of phenomena (dharmatā).
Then Śakra, Lord of the Devas, said this to the Blessed One:
"How, Blessed One, does the Elder Subhūti not contradict conventional designation while yet teaching the true nature of phenomena?"
When this had been said, the Blessed One spoke thus to Śakra, the lord of the gods:
"Kauśika, form is a mere designation; that which is a mere designation is the true nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*), and that the Elder Subhūti teaches without contradiction.
Sensation, Kauśika, is a mere designation; that which is a mere designation is the true nature of phenomena, and that the Elder Subhūti teaches without contradiction."

“Kauśika, perception is a mere designation; that which is a mere designation is the true nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*), and the Elder Subhūti teaches it without contradiction. Formations (*saṃskāra*) are a mere designation; that which is a mere designation is the true nature of phenomena, and the Elder Subhūti teaches it without contradiction.
Consciousness (*vijñāna*) is a mere designation; that which is a mere designation is the true nature of phenomena, and the Elder Subhūti teaches it without contradiction. Why is that?”
Kauśika, that which is the true nature (*dharmatā*) of phenomena is neither obstructed nor contradicted;
that which is neither obstructed nor contradicted is what the Elder Subhūti teaches, and he does not contradict it.
Kauśika, the eye is a mere designation (*prajñaptimātra*); that which is a mere designation is the true nature of phenomena, and the Elder Subhūti teaches it without contradiction.
The ear, Kauśika, is a mere designation; that which is a mere designation is the true nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*), and the Elder Subhūti teaches it without contradiction.
The nose, Kauśika, is a mere designation; that which is a mere designation is the true nature of phenomena, and the Elder Subhūti teaches it without contradiction.
The tongue, Kauśika, is a mere designation; that which is a mere designation is the true nature of phenomena, and the Elder Subhūti teaches it without contradiction.
The body, Kauśika, is a mere designation; that which is a mere designation is the true nature of phenomena (dharmatā), and the Elder Subhūti teaches it without contradiction.
The mind, Kauśika, is a mere designation; that which is a mere designation is the true nature of phenomena, and the Elder Subhūti teaches it without contradiction. Why is that?
Because that which is the true nature of phenomena, Kauśika, neither grows nor diminishes.
That which is neither obstructed nor opposed, that is what the Elder Subhūti teaches, and he does not oppose it.
Form, Kauśika, is a mere designation; that which is a mere designation is the true nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*), and the Elder Subhūti teaches that without opposition.
Sound, Kauśika, is a mere designation; that which is a mere designation is the true nature of phenomena, and the Elder Subhūti teaches that without opposition.
O Kauśika, smell is a mere designation; that which is a mere designation is the true nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*), and the Elder Subhūti teaches it without contradiction.
O Kauśika, taste is a mere designation; that which is a mere designation is the true nature of phenomena, and the Elder Subhūti teaches it without contradiction.
O Kauśika, touch is a mere designation; that which is a mere designation is the true nature of phenomena, and the Elder Subhūti teaches it without contradiction.
"Kauśika, all phenomena are mere designations; that which is a mere designation is the true nature of phenomena (dharmatā). The Elder Subhūti teaches this without contradiction.
Why is that?
Because, Kauśika, that which is the true nature of phenomena neither arises nor ceases."
That which neither conforms nor contradicts—that is what the Elder Subhūti teaches, and he does not contradict it.
O Kauśika, visual consciousness is a mere designation; that which is a mere designation is the true nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*). That is what the Elder Subhūti teaches without contradiction.

Gustatory consciousness, Kauśika, is a mere designation; that which is a mere designation is the true nature of phenomena, and the Elder Subhūti teaches it without contradiction.
Bodily consciousness, Kauśika, is a mere designation; that which is a mere designation is the true nature of phenomena (dharmatā), and the Elder Subhūti teaches it without contradiction.
Mental consciousness, Kauśika, is a mere designation; that which is a mere designation is the true nature of phenomena, and the Elder Subhūti teaches it without contradiction.
For what reason is that so?
Kauśika, that which is the true nature (*dharmatā*) of phenomena is neither obstructed nor contradicted;
and that which is neither obstructed nor contradicted, that is what the Elder Subhūti teaches without contradiction.

Kauśika, visual contact (*cakṣuḥ-saṃsparśa*) is a mere designation (*prajñapti-mātra*); and that which is a mere designation is the true nature of phenomena—this is what the Elder Subhūti teaches without contradiction.

O Kauśika, gustatory contact is a mere designation; that which is a mere designation is the true nature of phenomena, and the Elder Subhūti teaches it without contradiction."
Bodily contact, Kauśika, is a mere designation; that which is a mere designation is the true nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*), and the Elder Subhūti teaches it without contradiction.

That which neither obstructs nor is obstructed is what the Elder Subhūti teaches, and he does not contradict it.

Kauśika, that which is the true nature (*dharmatā*) of phenomena is neither obstructed nor contradicted;

Kauśika, the perfection of giving is a mere designation (*prajñaptimātra*); and that which is a mere designation is the true nature of phenomena, which the Elder Subhūti teaches without contradiction.

The perfection of wisdom, Kauśika, is a mere designation; that which is a mere designation is the true nature of phenomena, and the Elder Subhūti teaches it without contradiction. Why is that?

Kauśika, arhatship is a mere designation; that which is a mere designation is the true nature of phenomena, and the Elder Subhūti teaches it without contradiction.
Kauśika, solitary enlightenment (*pratyekabodhi*) is a mere designation...”
That *dharmatā* is mere designation; the Elder Subhūti teaches it without contradiction.
O Kauśika, the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*) is mere designation; that which is mere designation is *dharmatā*, and the Elder Subhūti teaches it without contradiction.
O Kauśika, the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*) is mere designation; that which is mere designation is *dharmatā*, and the Elder Subhūti teaches it without contradiction.
For what reason?
O Kauśika, that which is the true nature (dharmatā) of phenomena is neither obstructed nor contradicted;
and that which is neither obstructed nor contradicted, it is this that the Elder Subhūti teaches, and he does not contradict it.
“Kauśika, the stream-enterer is a mere designation; that which is a mere designation is the true nature of phenomena (dharmatā), and the Elder Subhūti teaches it without contradiction.
Kauśika, the once-returner is a mere designation; that which is a mere designation is the true nature of phenomena, and the Elder Subhūti teaches it without contradiction.
Kauśika, the non-returner is a mere designation; that which is a mere designation is the true nature of phenomena, and the Elder Subhūti teaches it without contradiction.”
"Kauśika, an Arhat is a mere designation; that which is a mere designation is the true nature of phenomena (dharmatā), and the Elder Subhūti teaches it without contradiction.
Kauśika, a Pratyekabuddha is a mere designation; that which is a mere designation is the true nature of phenomena, and the Elder Subhūti teaches it without contradiction.
Kauśika, a Bodhisattva is a mere designation; that which is a mere designation is the true nature of phenomena, and the Elder Subhūti teaches it without contradiction."
“Kauśika, the Perfectly Awakened One is a mere designation; that which is a mere designation is the true nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*). The Elder Subhūti teaches this without contradiction.
Why is that?
Because, Kauśika, that which is the true nature of phenomena is neither obstructed nor contradicted.”

That which is neither obstructed nor opposed—that is what the Elder Subhūti teaches, and he does not oppose it. In this way indeed, Kauśika, the Elder Subhūti does not oppose conventional designation.
Then the Venerable Subhūti said this to Śakra, the lord of the gods:
"So it is, Kauśika, so it is."

Just as the Blessed One has taught that all phenomena are mere designations, so indeed, Kauśika, a bodhisattva mahāsattva, having understood all phenomena to be mere designations, should train in the perfection of wisdom. Training in this way, moreover, Kauśika, a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not train in form. Why is that?
For he does not perceive form in that wherein he trains. He does not train in feeling. Why is that?
For he does not perceive feeling in that wherein he trains. He does not train in perception. Why is that?
For he does not perceive perception in that wherein he trains. He does not train in mental formations. Why is that?
For he does not perceive those formative forces (*saṃskāra*) wherein he trains; he does not train in consciousness (*vijñāna*). Why is that?
For he does not perceive that consciousness wherein he trains.
Training in this way, the bodhisattva mahāsattva does not train in the eye. Why is that?
Because he does not perceive an eye in which to train. He does not train in the ear. Why is that?
Because he does not perceive an ear in which to train. He does not train in the nose. Why is that?
For he does not perceive the nose wherein he trains; he does not train in the tongue. Why is that?
For he does not perceive the tongue wherein he trains. He does not train in the body. Why is that?
For he does not perceive the body wherein he trains. He does not train in the mind. Why is that?
For he does not perceive a mind wherein he trains.
Training in this way, the bodhisattva mahāsattva does not train in form. Why is that?
For he does not perceive form in that wherein he trains. He does not train in sound. Why is that?
For he does not perceive sound in that wherein he trains. He does not train in odor. Why is that?
For he does not perceive odor in that wherein he trains. He does not train in taste. Why is that?
For he does not perceive that taste in which he trains. He does not train in contact. Why is that?
Because he does not perceive that contact in which he trains. He does not train in phenomena (*dharmas*). Why is that?
Because he does not perceive those phenomena in which he trains.
Training in this way, the bodhisattva mahāsattva does not train in eye-consciousness. Why is that?
Because he does not perceive the eye-consciousness in which he might train. He does not train in ear-consciousness. Why is that?
Because he does not perceive the ear-consciousness in which he might train. He does not train in nose-consciousness. Why is that?
For he does not perceive the nose-consciousness in which he trains; he does not train in tongue-consciousness. Why is that?
For he does not perceive the tongue-consciousness in which he trains. He does not train in body-consciousness. Why is that?
For he does not perceive the body-consciousness in which he trains. He does not train in mind-consciousness. Why is that?
For he does not perceive the mental consciousness in which he trains.
Training in this way, the bodhisattva mahāsattva does not train in eye-contact. Why is that?
Because he does not perceive the eye-contact in which he trains. He does not train in ear-contact. Why is that?

For he does not perceive that ear-contact in which he trains. He does not train in nose-contact. Why is that? For he does not perceive that nose-contact in which he trains. He does not train in tongue-contact. Why is that? For he... [does not perceive that tongue-contact in which he trains]. (ŚsP_II-3_70)
He does not perceive the contact of the tongue wherein he trains; he does not train in the contact of the body. Why is that?
Because he does not perceive the contact of the body wherein he trains. He does not train in the contact of the mind. Why is that?
Because he does not perceive the contact of the mind wherein he trains.

Training in this way, the bodhisattva mahāsattva does not train in the feeling conditioned by eye-contact. Why is that? Because he does not perceive that feeling conditioned by eye-contact in which he might train. He does not train in the feeling conditioned by ear-contact. Why is that?
Because he does not perceive that feeling conditioned by ear-contact in which he might train. He does not train in the feeling conditioned by nose-contact. Why is that?
For he does not perceive the feeling conditioned by olfactory contact in that wherein he trains. He does not train in the feeling conditioned by gustatory contact;
why is that?
For he does not perceive the feeling conditioned by gustatory contact in that wherein he trains. He does not train in the feeling conditioned by tactile contact. Why is that?
For he does not perceive that feeling conditioned by bodily contact in which he trains; he does not train in the feeling conditioned by mental contact. Why is that?
Because he does not perceive that feeling conditioned by mental contact in which he trains.
Training in this way, the bodhisattva mahāsattva does not train in the earth element. Why is that?
For he does not perceive the earth element in which he trains; he does not train in the water element. Why is that?
Because he does not perceive the water element in which he trains. He does not train in the fire element. Why is that?
Because he does not perceive the fire element in which he trains. He does not train in the wind element. Why is that?
For he does not perceive the wind element in which he trains; he does not train in the space element. Why is that?
For he does not perceive the space element in which he trains. He does not train in the consciousness element. Why is that?
For he does not perceive the consciousness element in which he trains.
Training in this way, the bodhisattva mahāsattva does not train in ignorance. Why is that?

Because he does not perceive ignorance as something in which he might train. He does not train in formative predispositions (*saṃskāra*). Why is that? Because he does not perceive formative predispositions as something in which he might train. He does not train in consciousness (*vijñāna*). Why is that?
For he does not perceive consciousness in that wherein he trains; he does not train in name-and-form. Why is that?
For he does not perceive name-and-form in that wherein he trains. He does not train in the six sense bases. Why is that?
For he does not perceive the six sense bases in that wherein he trains. He does not train in contact. Why is that?
For he does not perceive that contact in which he trains. He does not train in feeling. Why is that?
For he does not perceive that feeling in which he trains. He does not train in craving. Why is that?
For just as he does not perceive craving in that wherein he trains, he does not train in grasping. Why is that?
Because he does not perceive grasping in that wherein he trains. He does not train in becoming. Why is that?
Because he does not perceive becoming in that wherein he trains. He does not train in birth. Why is that?
For he does not perceive birth wherein he trains; he does not train in old age and death. Why is that?
Because he does not perceive old age and death wherein he trains.
Training in this way, the bodhisattva mahāsattva does not train in the perfection of generosity. Why is that?
For he does not perceive the perfection of giving in which he trains; he does not train in the perfection of ethical discipline. Why is that?
For he does not perceive the perfection of ethical discipline in which he trains. He does not train in the perfection of patience. Why is that?
For he does not perceive the perfection of patience in which he trains. He does not train in the perfection of vigor. Why is that?
For he does not perceive the perfection of vigor wherein he trains; he does not train in the perfection of meditation. Why is that?
For he does not perceive the perfection of meditation wherein he trains. He does not train in the perfection of wisdom. Why is that?
For he does not perceive the perfection of wisdom wherein he trains.
Training in this way, the bodhisattva mahāsattva does not train in internal emptiness. Why is that?
Because he does not perceive that internal emptiness in which he might train. He does not train in external emptiness. Why is that?
Because he does not perceive that external emptiness in which he might train. He does not train in internal-and-external emptiness. Why is that?
For he does not perceive internal-and-external emptiness (*adhyātmabahirdhāśūnyatā*) wherein he might train. He does not train in the emptiness of emptiness (*śūnyatāśūnyatā*). Why is that?
For he does not perceive the emptiness of emptiness wherein he might train. He does not train in great emptiness (*mahāśūnyatā*). Why is that?
For he does not perceive great emptiness wherein he might train. He does not train in the emptiness of the ultimate truth (*paramārthaśūnyatā*). Why is that?
For he does not perceive that ultimate emptiness in which he trains. He does not train in conditioned emptiness. Why is that?
For he does not perceive that conditioned emptiness in which he trains. He does not train in unconditioned emptiness. Why is that?
For he does not perceive that unconditioned emptiness in which he trains. He does not train in absolute emptiness. Why is that?

For he does not perceive the emptiness of the ultimate (*atyantaśūnyatā*) wherein he might train. He does not train in the emptiness of that which is without beginning or end (*anavarāgraśūnyatā*). Why is that? For he does not perceive the emptiness of that which is without beginning or end wherein he might train. He does not train in the emptiness of non-dispersal (*anavakāraśūnyatā*). Why is that?

For he does not perceive non-repudiation emptiness (*anavakāra-śūnyatā*) wherein he might train. He does not train in natural emptiness (*prakṛti-śūnyatā*). Why is that? Because he does not perceive natural emptiness wherein he might train. He does not train in the emptiness of all phenomena (*sarvadharma-śūnyatā*). Why is that?
Because he does not perceive the emptiness of all phenomena wherein he might train. He does not train in the emptiness of specific characteristics (*svalakṣaṇa-śūnyatā*). Why is that?

For he does not perceive the emptiness of specific characteristics (*svalakṣaṇa-śūnyatā*) wherein he trains; he does not train in the emptiness of non-apprehension (*anupalambha-śūnyatā*). Why is that?
Because he does not perceive the emptiness of non-apprehension wherein he trains. He does not train in the emptiness of non-existence (*abhāva-śūnyatā*). Why is that?
Because he does not perceive the emptiness of non-existence wherein he trains. He does not train in the emptiness of intrinsic nature (*svabhāva-śūnyatā*). Why is that?
For he does not perceive that intrinsic emptiness in which he trains; he does not train in the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence. Why is that?
Because he does not perceive that emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence in which he trains.
Training in this manner, a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not train in the four foundations of mindfulness. Why is that?
For he does not perceive the four foundations of mindfulness in which he trains; he does not train in the four right efforts. Why is that?
Because he does not perceive the right efforts in which he trains. He does not train in the four bases of psychic power. Why is that?
Because he does not perceive the bases of psychic power in which he trains. He does not train in the five faculties. Why is that?
For he does not perceive the sense faculties in that wherein he trains. He does not train in the five powers. Why is that?
For he does not perceive the powers in that wherein he trains. He does not train in the seven factors of enlightenment. Why is that?
For he does not perceive the factors of enlightenment in that wherein he trains. He does not train in the noble eightfold path. Why is that?
For he does not perceive that Noble Eightfold Path in which he trains.
Training in this manner, the bodhisattva mahāsattva does not train in the four noble truths. Why is that?
Because he does not perceive those noble truths in which he trains. He does not train in the four meditative concentrations (*dhyāna*). Why is that?
For he does not perceive those meditative concentrations (*dhyāna*) in which he trains. He does not train in the four immeasurables (*apramāṇa*). Why is that?
For he does not perceive those immeasurables in which he trains. He does not train in the four formless attainments (*ārūpyasamāpatti*). Why is that?
For he does not perceive those formless attainments in which he trains. He does not train in the eight liberations (*vimokṣa*). Why is that?
For he does not perceive those eight liberations in which he trains. He does not train in the nine successive attainments of meditative dwelling. Why is that?

For he does not perceive those successive attainments of meditative dwelling in which he trains. He does not train in the gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness. Why is that?
For he does not perceive the gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—in which he might train. He does not train in the five superknowledges (*abhijñā*). Why is that?

Because he does not perceive those superknowledges in which he might train. He does not train in all meditative concentrations (*samādhi*). Why is that? Because he does not perceive any meditative concentrations in which he might train. He does not train in the gateways of mnemonic formulas (*dhāraṇīmukha*). Why is that?
For he does not perceive those gateways of dhāraṇī in which he trains. He does not train in the ten powers of a Tathāgata. Why is that?
Because he does not perceive those ten powers of a Tathāgata in which he trains. He does not train in the four grounds of self-confidence. Why is that?
Because he does not perceive those grounds of self-confidence in which he trains. He does not train in the four analytical knowledges. Why is that?
For he does not perceive the four analytical knowledges (*pratisaṃvid*) in which he trains. He does not train in great loving-kindness (*mahāmaitrī*). Why is that?
Because he does not perceive great loving-kindness in which he trains. He does not train in great compassion (*mahākaruṇā*). Why is that?
Because he does not perceive great compassion in which he trains. He does not train in the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha (*āveṇikabuddhadharma*). Why is that?
For he does not perceive those eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha in which he trains.
Training in this way, a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not train for the fruit of stream-entry. Why is that?
Because he does not perceive the fruit of stream-entry in which he trains. He does not train for the fruit of once-returning. Why is that?
For he does not perceive the fruit of once-returning wherein he trains. He does not train for the fruit of non-returning. Why is that?
For he does not perceive the fruit of non-returning wherein he trains. He does not train for arhatship. Why is that?
For he does not perceive arhatship wherein he trains. He does not train for solitary enlightenment. Why is that?
For he does not perceive that pratyekabuddha-enlightenment in which he trains. He does not train in the knowledge of the aspects of the path. Why is that?
Because he does not perceive that knowledge of the aspects of the path in which he trains. He does not train in the knowledge of all aspects. Why is that?
Because he does not perceive that knowledge of all aspects in which he trains.
Then Śakra, the lord of the gods, said this to the elder Subhūti:
"For what reason, venerable Subhūti, does a bodhisattva mahāsattva not perceive form? For what reason does he not perceive feeling?"
For what reason does one not perceive perception?
For what reason does one not perceive mental formations?
For what reason does one not perceive consciousness?
For what reason does the eye not perceive? For what reason does the ear not perceive?
For what reason does the nose not perceive?
For what reason does he not perceive the tongue?
For what reason does he not perceive the body?
For what reason does he not perceive the mind?
For what reason does one not perceive form?
For what reason does one not perceive sound?
For what reason does one not perceive odor?
For what reason does one not perceive taste?
For what reason does one not perceive touch?
For what reason does one not perceive mental phenomena?
For what reason does visual consciousness not perceive?
For what reason does auditory consciousness not perceive?
For what reason does olfactory consciousness not perceive?
For what reason does one not perceive tongue-consciousness?
For what reason does one not perceive body-consciousness?
For what reason does one not perceive mind-consciousness?
For what reason does he not perceive eye-contact?
For what reason does he not perceive ear-contact?
For what reason does he not perceive nose-contact?
For what reason does one not perceive tongue-contact?
For what reason does one not perceive body-contact?
For what reason does one not perceive mind-contact?
For what reason does one not perceive feeling conditioned by eye-contact?
For what reason does one not perceive feeling conditioned by ear-contact?
For what reason does one not perceive feeling conditioned by nose-contact?
For what reason does one not perceive feeling conditioned by tongue-contact?
For what reason does one not perceive feeling conditioned by body-contact?
For what reason does one not perceive feeling conditioned by mind-contact?
For what reason does one not perceive the earth element?
For what reason does one not perceive the water element?
For what reason does one not perceive the fire element?
For what reason does one not perceive the wind element?
For what reason does one not perceive the space element?
For what reason does one not perceive the consciousness element?
For what reason does one not perceive ignorance?
For what reason does one not perceive formative forces?
For what reason does one not perceive consciousness?
For what reason does one not perceive name-and-form?
For what reason does one not perceive the six sense bases?
For what reason does one not perceive contact?
For what reason does one not perceive feeling?
For what reason does one not perceive craving? For what reason does one not perceive grasping?
He does not perceive it;
for what reason does he not perceive becoming,
and for what reason does he not perceive birth?
For what reason does one not perceive old age and death?
For what reason does one not perceive the perfection of generosity? For what reason does one not perceive the perfection of ethical discipline?
For what reason does one not perceive the perfection of patience?
For what reason does one not perceive the perfection of vigor? For what reason does one not perceive the perfection of meditative concentration?
For what reason does one not perceive the perfection of wisdom?
For what reason does one not perceive internal emptiness?
For what reason does one not perceive external emptiness?
For what reason does one not perceive internal-external emptiness?
For what reason does one not perceive the emptiness of emptiness?
For what reason does one not perceive great emptiness?
For what reason does one not perceive the emptiness of the ultimate truth?
For what reason does one not perceive the emptiness of the conditioned?
For what reason does one not perceive the emptiness of the unconditioned?
For what reason does one not perceive absolute emptiness?
For what reason does one not perceive the emptiness of the beginningless and endless?
For what reason does one not perceive the emptiness of non-dispersal?
For what reason does one not perceive the emptiness of intrinsic nature?
For what reason does one not perceive the emptiness of all phenomena?
For what reason does one not perceive the emptiness of specific characteristics?
For what reason does one not perceive the emptiness of non-apprehension?
For what reason does one not perceive the emptiness of non-existence?
For what reason does one not perceive the emptiness of intrinsic nature?
For what reason does he not perceive the emptiness of the nature of non-existence?
For what reason does he not perceive the foundations of mindfulness?
For what reason does he not perceive the right efforts?
For what reason does he not perceive the bases of psychic power?
For what reason does he not perceive the faculties?
For what reason does he not perceive the powers?
For what reason does one not perceive the factors of enlightenment?
For what reason does one not perceive the noble eightfold path?
For what reason does one not perceive the noble truths?
For what reason does one not perceive the meditative absorptions? For what reason does one not perceive the immeasurables? For what reason does one not perceive the formless attainments?
For what reason does he not perceive the eight liberations? For what reason does he not perceive the nine successive attainments of meditative dwelling?
For what reason does one not perceive the gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness?
For what reason does one not perceive the superknowledges?
For what reason does one not perceive the meditative concentrations?
For what reason does he not perceive the gateways of dhāraṇī?
For what reason does he not perceive the ten powers of a Tathāgata?
For what reason does he not perceive the four grounds of self-confidence?
For what reason does he not perceive the four analytical knowledges? For what reason does he not perceive great loving-kindness?
For what reason does one not perceive great compassion?
For what reason does one not perceive the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha?
For what reason does one not perceive omniscience?
"For what reason does one not perceive the knowledge of the aspects of the path?
For what reason does one not perceive the knowledge of all aspects?
Subhūti replied:
For in this way, Kauśika, form is empty of form; feeling is empty of feeling;
perception is empty of perception.
Formations are empty of formations;
consciousness is empty of consciousness.
The eye is empty of the eye.
The ear is empty of the ear; the nose is empty of the nose;
the tongue is empty of the tongue.
The body is empty of the body;
the mind is empty of the mind. Form is empty of form.
Sound is empty of sound; odor is empty of odor;
taste is empty of taste.
Contact is empty of contact; phenomena are empty of phenomena.
Eye-consciousness is empty of eye-consciousness.
Ear-consciousness is empty of ear-consciousness;
nose-consciousness is empty of nose-consciousness;
tongue-consciousness is empty of ear-consciousness.
Body-consciousness is empty of body-consciousness;
mind-consciousness is empty of mind-consciousness. Eye-contact is empty of eye-contact.
Auditory contact is empty of auditory contact; olfactory contact is empty of olfactory contact;
gustatory contact is empty of gustatory contact.
Body-contact is empty of body-contact; mind-contact is empty of mind-contact.
Feeling born of eye-contact is empty of feeling born of eye-contact.
Feeling born of ear-contact is empty of feeling born of ear-contact; feeling born of nose-contact is empty of feeling born of nose-contact;
feeling born of tongue-contact is empty of feeling born of tongue-contact.
Feeling born of body-contact is empty of feeling born of body-contact; feeling born of mind-contact is empty of feeling born of mind-contact.
The earth element is empty of the earth element.
The water element is empty of the water element;
the fire element is empty of the fire element;
the air element is empty of the air element.
The space element is empty of the space element;
the consciousness element is empty of the earth element.
Ignorance is empty of ignorance.
Formations are empty of formations; consciousness is empty of consciousness;
name-and-form is empty of name-and-form.
The six sense bases are empty of the six sense bases; contact is empty of contact;
feeling is empty of feeling.
Craving is empty of craving; grasping is empty of grasping;
becoming is empty of becoming.
Birth is empty of birth; old age and death are empty of old age and death.
The perfection of generosity is empty of the perfection of generosity.
The perfection of ethical discipline is empty of the perfection of ethical discipline;
the perfection of patience is empty of the perfection of patience;
the perfection of vigor is empty of the perfection of vigor.
The perfection of meditation is empty of the perfection of meditation;
the perfection of wisdom is empty of the perfection of wisdom.
Internal emptiness is empty of internal emptiness.
External emptiness is empty of external emptiness;
internal-external emptiness is empty of internal-external emptiness;
the emptiness of emptiness is empty of the emptiness of emptiness.
Great emptiness is empty of great emptiness;
ultimate emptiness is empty of ultimate emptiness;
conditioned emptiness is empty of conditioned emptiness.
Unconditioned emptiness is empty of unconditioned emptiness;
absolute emptiness is empty of absolute emptiness;
emptiness without beginning or end is empty of emptiness without beginning or end.
Non-dispersal emptiness is empty of non-dispersal emptiness;
essential nature emptiness is empty of essential nature emptiness;
the emptiness of all phenomena is empty of the emptiness of all phenomena.
The emptiness of specific characteristics is empty of the emptiness of specific characteristics;
the emptiness of non-apprehension is empty of internal emptiness;
the emptiness of non-existence is empty of internal emptiness.
The emptiness of intrinsic nature is empty of the emptiness of intrinsic nature;
the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence is empty of internal emptiness.
The applications of mindfulness are empty of the applications of mindfulness.
The right efforts are empty of right efforts; the bases of psychic power are empty of bases of psychic power;
the faculties are empty of faculties.
The powers are empty of powers; the factors of enlightenment are empty of factors of enlightenment;
the noble eightfold path is empty of the noble eightfold path.
The noble truths are empty of the noble truths; the meditative absorptions are empty of the meditative absorptions;
the immeasurables are empty of the immeasurables.
The formless attainments are empty of formless attainments;
the liberations are empty of liberations;
the serial attainments are empty of serial attainments.
The doors of liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—are empty of the doors of liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness;
the superknowledges are empty of the superknowledges;
the meditative concentrations are empty of the meditative concentrations.
The gateways of dhāraṇī are empty of the gateways of dhāraṇī; the ten powers of a Tathāgata are empty of the ten powers of a Tathāgata;
the grounds of self-confidence are empty of the grounds of self-confidence.
The analytical knowledges are empty of the analytical knowledges; great loving-kindness is empty of great loving-kindness;
great compassion is empty of great compassion.
The unique qualities of a Buddha are empty of the unique qualities of a Buddha;
omniscience is empty of omniscience; and the knowledge of the aspects of the path is empty of the knowledge of the aspects of the path.
It is empty; omniscience is empty of omniscience.
For indeed, Kauśika, the emptiness of form does not perceive the emptiness of form, nor does the emptiness of feeling perceive the emptiness of feeling.
The emptiness of perception does not perceive the emptiness of perception;
the emptiness of formations does not perceive the emptiness of formations;
the emptiness of consciousness does not perceive the emptiness of consciousness.
The emptiness of the eye does not perceive the emptiness of the eye;
the emptiness of the ear does not perceive the emptiness of the ear;
the emptiness of the nose does not perceive the emptiness of the nose.
The emptiness of the tongue does not perceive the emptiness of the tongue;
the emptiness of the body does not perceive the emptiness of the body;
the emptiness of the mind does not perceive the emptiness of the mind.
The emptiness of form does not perceive the emptiness of form;
the emptiness of sound does not perceive the emptiness of sound;
the emptiness of odor does not perceive the emptiness of odor.
The emptiness of taste does not perceive the emptiness of taste;
the emptiness of contact does not perceive the emptiness of contact;
the emptiness of phenomena does not perceive the emptiness of phenomena.
The emptiness of eye-consciousness does not perceive the emptiness of eye-consciousness;
the emptiness of ear-consciousness does not perceive the emptiness of ear-consciousness;
the emptiness of nose-consciousness does not perceive the emptiness of nose-consciousness.
Tongueness-of-consciousness does not perceive the emptiness of tongue-consciousness; body-consciousness does not perceive the emptiness of body-consciousness;
and mind-consciousness does not perceive the emptiness of mind-consciousness.
The emptiness of eye-contact does not perceive the emptiness of perception; the emptiness of ear-contact does not perceive the emptiness of perception;
the emptiness of nose-contact does not perceive the emptiness of perception.
The emptiness of tongue-contact does not perceive the emptiness of perception;
the emptiness of body-contact does not perceive the emptiness of perception;
the emptiness of mind-contact does not perceive the emptiness of perception.

The emptiness of feeling conditioned by eye-contact does not perceive the emptiness of feeling conditioned by eye-contact; the emptiness of feeling conditioned by ear-contact does not perceive the emptiness of feeling conditioned by ear-contact;
the emptiness of feeling conditioned by nose-contact does not perceive the emptiness of feeling conditioned by nose-contact.
The emptiness of feeling conditioned by tongue-contact does not perceive the emptiness of feeling conditioned by tongue-contact;

the emptiness of feeling conditioned by body-contact does not perceive the emptiness of feeling conditioned by body-contact; the emptiness of feeling conditioned by mind-contact does not perceive the emptiness of feeling conditioned by mind-contact.
