"By means of internal-external emptiness (*adhyātmabahirdhāśūnyatā*).
In this way indeed, Venerable Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva will set forth toward all-aspect omniscience (*sarvākārajñatā*) through the application of grasping no dharmas at all.
He said: "Venerable Subhūti, a bodhisattva mahāsattva training in this manner, by abiding in the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*), will set forth toward all-aspect omniscience."
Subhūti said:

"Venerable Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva training in this way, abiding in the perfection of wisdom, will emerge into the knowledge of all aspects by means of not grasping at any phenomena."

He asked: "Venerable Subhūti, if a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in this way—having trained for the sake of grasping and for the sake of the disappearance of all dharmas—how will he emerge into the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*)?
Subhūti replied:
"In this regard, venerable Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom does not perceive the arising of form."

One does not perceive cessation, nor does one perceive grasping, nor does one perceive relinquishment; one does not perceive affliction, nor does one perceive purification; one does not perceive accumulation, nor does one perceive diminution; one does not perceive decrease, nor does one perceive increase. For what reason?
For in this way, form does not exist and is not perceived within the intrinsic nature of form;
one does not see the arising of feeling, nor does one see its cessation, nor does one see its grasping, nor does one see its relinquishing,
nor does one see its affliction, nor does one see its purification, nor does one see its accumulation, nor does one see its diminution, nor does one see its decrease.
He does not see increase; he does not see decrease. For what reason?
Because feeling does not exist and is not perceived within the intrinsic nature of feeling;
he does not see the arising of perception, nor does he see its cessation, nor does he see its grasping, nor does he see its relinquishing.
He perceives neither affliction nor purification; he perceives neither accumulation nor diminution; he perceives neither decrease nor increase. Why is that?
Because perception does not exist and is not apprehended within the intrinsic nature of perception.
One does not perceive the arising of conditioned phenomena, nor does one perceive their cessation; one does not perceive grasping, nor does one perceive relinquishing;

one does not perceive affliction, nor does one perceive purification; one does not perceive accumulation, nor does one perceive diminution; one does not perceive decrease, nor does one perceive increase. Why is that?
For in this way, formations do not exist and are not perceived within the intrinsic nature of formations;
one does not perceive the arising of consciousness, nor does one perceive its cessation; one does not perceive grasping, nor does one perceive relinquishing;
one does not perceive affliction, nor does one perceive purification; one does not perceive accumulation, nor does one perceive diminution, nor does one perceive loss.
He does not see increase; he does not see decrease. Why is that?
Because consciousness does not exist and is not apprehended within the intrinsic nature of consciousness.
He does not see the arising of the eye, nor does he see its cessation; he does not see its grasping, nor does he see its relinquishing.

One does not perceive affliction, nor does one perceive purification; one does not perceive accumulation, nor does one perceive diminution; one does not perceive decrease, nor does one perceive increase. Why is that?
Because the eye does not exist and is not apprehended within the intrinsic nature of the eye.
One does not see the arising of the ear, nor does one see its cessation; one does not see its grasping, nor its relinquishing;
one does not see its defilement, nor its purification; one does not see its accumulation, nor its diminution; one does not see its decrease, nor its increase. Why is that?
For in this way, the ear does not exist and is not perceived within the intrinsic nature of the ear;
it does not see the arising of the nose, nor does it see its cessation; it does not see grasping, nor does it see relinquishing;
it does not see affliction, nor does it see purification; it does not see accumulation, nor does it see diminution; it does not see decrease.
He does not see increase; he does not see [decrease]. For what reason?
Because the nose does not exist and is not perceived in the intrinsic nature of the nose;
he does not see the arising of the tongue, he does not see its cessation, nor does he see its grasping.

He does not perceive relinquishment, he does not perceive affliction, he does not perceive purification; he does not perceive accumulation, he does not perceive diminution; he does not perceive decrease, he does not perceive increase. Why is that?
Because, in this way, the tongue does not exist and is not apprehended within the intrinsic nature of the tongue.
He does not perceive the arising of the body, he does not perceive its cessation; he does not perceive grasping, nor does he perceive relinquishment.
He perceives neither affliction nor purification; he perceives neither accumulation nor diminution; he perceives neither decrease nor increase. Why is that?
Because the body does not exist and is not apprehended within the intrinsic nature of the body.
One does not perceive the arising of the mind, nor does one perceive its cessation; one does not perceive grasping, nor does one perceive relinquishing;

one does not perceive affliction, nor does one perceive purification; one does not perceive accumulation, nor does one perceive diminution; one does not perceive decrease, nor does one perceive increase. Why is that?
For in this way, the mind does not exist and is not apprehended within the intrinsic nature of the mind.

It does not perceive the arising of form, nor does it perceive its cessation; it does not perceive grasping, nor does it perceive relinquishing; it does not perceive affliction, nor does it perceive purification.
He perceives neither accumulation nor depletion; he perceives neither decrease nor increase. Why is that?
Because form does not exist and is not apprehended within the intrinsic nature of form;
he does not perceive the arising of sound.
He does not perceive cessation, nor does he perceive grasping, nor does he perceive relinquishment; he does not perceive affliction, nor does he perceive purification;
he does not perceive accumulation, nor does he perceive diminution; he does not perceive decrease, nor does he perceive increase. Why is that?
Because sound does not exist and is not apprehended within the intrinsic nature of sound.

One does not see the arising of odor, nor does one see its cessation; one does not see its grasping, nor its relinquishing; one does not see its defilement, nor its purification; one does not see its accumulation, nor its diminution; one does not see its decrease, nor its increase. Why is that?
For in this way, smell does not exist and is not perceived within the intrinsic nature of smell;
one does not see the arising of taste,
nor does one see its cessation, nor does one see its grasping, nor does one see its relinquishing, nor does one see its affliction, nor does one see its purification.
He perceives neither accumulation nor diminution; he perceives neither loss nor increase. Why is that?
Because taste does not exist and is not apprehended within the intrinsic nature of taste;
he does not perceive the arising of touch.

He does not perceive cessation, he does not perceive grasping, he does not perceive relinquishment, he does not perceive affliction, he does not perceive purification, he does not perceive accumulation, he does not perceive diminution, he does not perceive decrease, and he does not perceive increase. Why is that?
Because contact does not exist and is not apprehended within the intrinsic nature of contact.

One does not perceive the arising of phenomena, nor does one perceive their cessation; one does not perceive grasping, nor does one perceive relinquishing; one does not perceive affliction, nor does one perceive purification; one does not perceive accumulation, nor does one perceive diminution; one does not perceive decrease, nor does one perceive increase.
He sees it. For what reason?
Because phenomena do not exist and are not apprehended within the intrinsic nature of phenomena.
He does not see the arising of visual consciousness.

One does not perceive cessation, one does not perceive grasping, one does not perceive relinquishment, one does not perceive affliction, one does not perceive purification, one does not perceive accumulation, one does not perceive diminution, one does not perceive decrease, and one does not perceive increase. Why is that?
Because visual consciousness does not exist and is not apprehended within the intrinsic nature of visual consciousness.

One does not perceive the arising of auditory consciousness, nor does one perceive its cessation; one does not perceive grasping, nor does one perceive relinquishing; one does not perceive affliction, nor does one perceive purification; one does not perceive accumulation, nor does one perceive diminution; one does not perceive decrease, nor does one perceive increase. For what reason?
For in this way, auditory consciousness does not exist and is not perceived within the intrinsic nature of auditory consciousness;
it does not see the arising of olfactory consciousness,
nor does it see its cessation, nor does it see grasping, nor does it see relinquishing, nor does it see affliction, nor does it see purification.
He perceives neither accumulation nor diminution; he perceives neither loss nor increase. Why is that?
Because olfactory consciousness does not exist and is not apprehended within the intrinsic nature of olfactory consciousness;
he does not perceive the arising of gustatory consciousness.

One does not perceive cessation, one does not perceive grasping, one does not perceive relinquishment, one does not perceive affliction, one does not perceive purification, one does not perceive accumulation, one does not perceive diminution, one does not perceive decrease, and one does not perceive increase. Why is that?
Because tongue-consciousness does not exist and is not apprehended within the intrinsic nature of tongue-consciousness.

He does not perceive the arising of body-consciousness, nor does he perceive its cessation; he does not perceive its grasping, nor its relinquishing; he does not perceive its defilement, nor its purification;
he does not perceive its accumulation, nor its diminution; he does not perceive its decrease, nor its increase. For what reason?
For in this way, body-consciousness does not exist and is not perceived within the intrinsic nature of body-consciousness;
it does not see the arising of mental consciousness,
nor does it see its cessation, nor does it see grasping, nor does it see relinquishing, nor does it see affliction, nor does it see purification.
He perceives neither accumulation nor diminution; he perceives neither loss nor increase. Why is that?
Because mental consciousness does not exist and is not apprehended within the intrinsic nature of mental consciousness.
He does not perceive the arising of visual contact.
He does not perceive cessation, he does not perceive grasping, he does not perceive relinquishment, he does not perceive affliction, he does not perceive purification;
he does not perceive accumulation, he does not perceive diminution, he does not perceive decrease, and he does not perceive increase. Why is that?
Because visual contact does not exist and is not apprehended within the intrinsic nature of visual contact.

One does not perceive the arising of ear-contact, nor does one perceive its cessation; one does not perceive grasping, nor does one perceive relinquishing; one does not perceive affliction, nor does one perceive purification;
one does not perceive accumulation, nor does one perceive diminution; one does not perceive decrease, nor does one perceive increase. Why is that?
For in this way, auditory contact does not exist and is not perceived within the intrinsic nature of auditory contact;
one does not see the arising of olfactory contact,
nor does one see its cessation, nor does one see its grasping, nor does one see its relinquishing, nor does one see its affliction, nor does one see its purification.
He perceives neither accumulation nor depletion; he perceives neither decrease nor increase. Why is that?
Because nose-contact does not exist and is not apprehended within the intrinsic nature of nose-contact;
he does not perceive the arising of tongue-contact.

One does not perceive cessation, one does not perceive grasping, one does not perceive relinquishment, one does not perceive affliction, one does not perceive purification, one does not perceive accumulation, one does not perceive diminution, one does not perceive decrease, and one does not perceive increase. Why is that?
Because tongue-contact does not exist and is not apprehended within the intrinsic nature of tongue-contact.

One does not perceive the arising of body-contact, nor does one perceive its cessation; one does not perceive its grasping, nor its relinquishing; one does not perceive its defilement, nor its purification; one does not perceive its accumulation, nor its diminution; one does not perceive its decrease, nor its increase. Why is that?
For in this way, bodily contact does not exist and is not perceived within the intrinsic nature of bodily contact;
one does not perceive the arising of mental contact,
nor its cessation, nor its grasping, nor its relinquishing, nor its affliction, nor its purification.
He sees neither accumulation nor diminution; he sees neither loss nor increase. Why is that?
Because mental contact does not exist and is not apprehended within the intrinsic nature of mental contact.
He does not see the arising of feeling conditioned by visual contact.

He does not perceive cessation, he does not perceive grasping, he does not perceive relinquishment, he does not perceive affliction, he does not perceive purification, he does not perceive accumulation, he does not perceive diminution, he does not perceive decrease, and he does not perceive increase. Why is that?
Because feeling conditioned by eye-contact does not exist and is not apprehended within the intrinsic nature of feeling conditioned by eye-contact.
He does not perceive the arising of feeling conditioned by auditory contact;

he does not perceive its cessation, nor its grasping, nor its relinquishing; he does not perceive defilement, nor purification; he does not perceive accumulation, nor diminution; he does not perceive decrease, nor increase. Why is that?
For in this way, feeling conditioned by ear-contact does not exist and is not apprehended within the intrinsic nature of feeling conditioned by ear-contact;
one does not see the arising of feeling conditioned by nose-contact,
nor does one see its cessation, nor does one see its grasping, nor does one see its relinquishing, nor does one see its affliction, nor does one see its purification.
He perceives neither accumulation nor diminution; he perceives neither loss nor increase. Why is that?
Because, in the intrinsic nature of feeling conditioned by nose-contact, that feeling conditioned by nose-contact does not exist and is not apprehended;
nor does he perceive the arising of feeling conditioned by tongue-contact.

One does not perceive cessation, one does not perceive grasping, one does not perceive relinquishment, one does not perceive affliction, one does not perceive purification, one does not perceive accumulation, one does not perceive diminution, one does not perceive decrease, and one does not perceive increase. Why is that?
Because feeling conditioned by tongue-contact does not exist and is not apprehended within the intrinsic nature of feeling conditioned by tongue-contact.
He does not perceive the arising of feeling conditioned by bodily contact;

he does not perceive its cessation, nor its grasping, nor its relinquishing; he does not perceive defilement, nor purification; he does not perceive accumulation, nor diminution; he does not perceive decrease, nor increase. Why is that?
For in this way, feeling conditioned by bodily contact does not exist and is not apprehended within the intrinsic nature of feeling conditioned by bodily contact;
one does not perceive the arising of feeling conditioned by mental contact,
nor its cessation, nor its grasping, nor its relinquishing, nor its defilement, nor its purification.
He perceives neither accumulation nor diminution; he perceives neither loss nor increase. Why is that?
Because feeling conditioned by mental contact does not exist and is not apprehended within the intrinsic nature of feeling conditioned by mental contact.
He does not perceive the arising of the earth element.

One does not perceive cessation, one does not perceive grasping, one does not perceive relinquishment, one does not perceive affliction, one does not perceive purification, one does not perceive accumulation, one does not perceive diminution, one does not perceive decrease, and one does not perceive increase. Why is that?
Because the earth element does not [exist] in the intrinsic nature of the earth element.
It exists, yet it is not apprehended;
one does not perceive the arising of the water element,
nor its cessation, nor its grasping, nor its relinquishing, nor its defilement, nor its purification, nor its accumulation, nor its diminution, nor its loss.
He does not see increase, he does not see decrease; for what reason?
Because the water element does not exist and is not apprehended within the intrinsic nature of the water element.

One does not perceive the arising of the fire element, nor does one perceive its cessation; one does not perceive its grasping, nor its relinquishing; one does not perceive its defilement, nor its purification;
one does not perceive its accumulation, nor its diminution; one does not perceive its decrease, nor its increase. Why is that?
For in this way, the fire element does not exist and is not perceived within the intrinsic nature of the fire element;
it does not perceive the arising of the wind element,
nor does it perceive its cessation, nor does it perceive grasping, nor does it perceive relinquishing, nor does it perceive affliction, nor does it perceive purification.
He perceives neither accumulation nor depletion; he perceives neither loss nor increase. Why is that?
Because the earth element does not exist and is not apprehended within the intrinsic nature of the earth element, nor does he perceive the arising of the space element.

He does not perceive cessation, he does not perceive grasping, he does not perceive relinquishment, he does not perceive affliction, he does not perceive purification, he does not perceive accumulation, he does not perceive diminution, he does not perceive decrease, and he does not perceive increase. Why is that?
Because the element of space does not exist and is not apprehended within the intrinsic nature of the element of space.

One does not perceive the arising of the consciousness element, nor does one perceive its cessation; one does not perceive grasping, nor does one perceive relinquishing; one does not perceive affliction, nor does one perceive purification; one does not perceive accumulation, nor does one perceive diminution; one does not perceive decrease, nor does one perceive increase. Why is that?
For thus, the consciousness element does not exist and is not apprehended within the intrinsic nature of the consciousness element.
One does not perceive the arising of ignorance, nor its cessation; one does not perceive grasping, nor relinquishment; one does not perceive affliction, nor purification.
He perceives neither accumulation nor depletion; he perceives neither decrease nor increase. Why is that?
Because ignorance does not exist and is not apprehended within the intrinsic nature of ignorance;
he does not perceive the arising of the formative forces (*saṃskāra*).

He does not perceive cessation, he does not perceive grasping, he does not perceive relinquishment, he does not perceive affliction, he does not perceive purification, he does not perceive accumulation, he does not perceive diminution, he does not perceive decrease, and he does not perceive increase. Why is that?
Because, in this way, conditioned phenomena do not exist within the intrinsic nature of conditioned phenomena.
It is not apprehended;
one does not see the arising of consciousness,
nor does one see its cessation, nor does one see its grasping, nor does one see its relinquishing, nor does one see its affliction, nor does one see its purification.
He perceives neither accumulation nor diminution; he perceives neither loss nor increase. Why is that?
Because consciousness does not exist and is not apprehended within the intrinsic nature of consciousness;
he does not perceive the arising of name-and-form.
He does not perceive cessation, nor does he perceive grasping, nor does he perceive relinquishment; he does not perceive affliction, nor does he perceive purification;
he does not perceive accumulation, nor does he perceive diminution; he does not perceive decrease, nor does he perceive increase. Why is that?
Because name-and-form does not exist and is not apprehended within the intrinsic nature of name-and-form.

One does not perceive the arising of the six sense bases, nor does one perceive their cessation; one does not perceive grasping, nor does one perceive relinquishing; one does not perceive affliction, nor does one perceive purification; one does not perceive accumulation, nor does one perceive diminution; one does not perceive decrease, nor does one perceive increase. Why is that?
For in this way, the six sense bases do not exist and are not perceived within the intrinsic nature of the six sense bases;
one does not see the arising of contact,
nor does one see its cessation, nor does one see its grasping, nor does one see its relinquishing, nor does one see its affliction, nor does one see its purification.
He perceives neither accumulation nor diminution; he perceives neither loss nor increase. Why is that?
Because contact does not exist and is not apprehended within the intrinsic nature of contact;
he does not perceive the arising of sensation.

One does not perceive cessation, one does not perceive grasping, one does not perceive relinquishment, one does not perceive affliction, one does not perceive purification, one does not perceive accumulation, one does not perceive diminution, one does not perceive decrease, and one does not perceive increase. Why is that?
Because feeling does not exist and is not apprehended within the intrinsic nature of feeling.

One does not perceive the arising of craving, nor does one perceive its cessation; one does not perceive grasping, nor does one perceive relinquishing; one does not perceive affliction, nor does one perceive purification; one does not perceive accumulation, nor does one perceive diminution; one does not perceive decrease, nor does one perceive increase. Why is that?
For in this way, craving does not exist and is not perceived within the intrinsic nature of craving;
one does not perceive the arising of grasping,
nor does one perceive its cessation, nor does one perceive its appropriation, nor does one perceive its relinquishment, nor does one perceive defilement, nor does one perceive purification.
He perceives neither accumulation nor depletion; he perceives neither decrease nor increase. Why is that?
Because grasping does not exist and is not apprehended within the intrinsic nature of grasping;
he does not perceive the arising of existence.
One does not perceive cessation, nor does one perceive grasping;

one does not perceive relinquishment, nor does one perceive affliction, nor does one perceive purification; one does not perceive accumulation, nor does one perceive diminution; one does not perceive decrease, nor does one perceive increase. Why is that?
Because, in this way, existence does not exist and is not apprehended within the intrinsic nature of existence.

One does not perceive the arising of birth, nor does one perceive its cessation; one does not perceive grasping, nor does one perceive relinquishing; one does not perceive affliction, nor does one perceive purification; one does not perceive accumulation, nor does one perceive diminution; one does not perceive decrease, nor does one perceive increase. Why is that?
For in this way, birth does not exist and is not perceived within the intrinsic nature of birth;
it does not see the arising of aging and death, nor does it see their cessation; it does not see grasping, nor does it see relinquishing; it does not see affliction, nor does it see purification.
He perceives neither accumulation nor depletion; he perceives neither loss nor increase. Why is that?
Because aging and death do not exist and are not apprehended within the intrinsic nature of aging and death.
He does not perceive the arising of the perfection of generosity.

He does not perceive cessation, he does not perceive grasping, he does not perceive relinquishment, he does not perceive affliction, he does not perceive purification, he does not perceive accumulation, he does not perceive diminution, he does not perceive decrease, and he does not perceive increase. Why is that?
Because the perfection of giving does not exist and is not apprehended within the intrinsic nature of the perfection of giving.
He does not perceive the arising of the perfection of ethical discipline;

he does not perceive its cessation, nor its grasping, nor its relinquishing; he does not perceive its defilement, nor its purification; he does not perceive its accumulation, nor its diminution; he does not perceive its decrease, nor its increase. Why is that?
For in this way, the perfection of ethical discipline does not exist and is not perceived in the intrinsic nature of the perfection of ethical discipline;
one does not perceive the arising of the perfection of patience, nor its cessation, nor its grasping, nor its relinquishing, nor its affliction, nor its purification.
He perceives neither accumulation nor diminution; he perceives neither loss nor increase. Why is that?
Because the perfection of patience does not exist and is not apprehended within the intrinsic nature of the perfection of patience;
he does not perceive the arising of the perfection of vigor.

He does not perceive cessation, he does not perceive grasping, he does not perceive relinquishment, he does not perceive affliction, he does not perceive purification, he does not perceive accumulation, he does not perceive diminution, he does not perceive decrease, and he does not perceive increase. Why is that?
Because the perfection of vigor does not exist and is not apprehended within the intrinsic nature of the perfection of vigor.

One does not perceive the arising of the perfection of meditation, nor does one perceive its cessation; one does not perceive its grasping, nor its relinquishing; one does not perceive its affliction, nor its purification; one does not perceive its accumulation, nor its diminution; one does not perceive its decrease, nor its increase. For what reason?
For in this way, the perfection of meditation does not exist and is not apprehended in the intrinsic nature of the perfection of meditation;
one does not perceive the arising of the perfection of wisdom, nor its cessation, nor its grasping, nor its relinquishing, nor its defilement, nor its purification.
He perceives neither accumulation nor diminution; he perceives neither loss nor increase. Why is that?
Because the perfection of wisdom does not exist and is not apprehended within the intrinsic nature of the perfection of wisdom.
He does not perceive the arising of internal emptiness.

He does not perceive cessation, he does not perceive grasping, he does not perceive relinquishment, he does not perceive affliction, he does not perceive purification, he does not perceive accumulation, he does not perceive diminution, he does not perceive decrease, and he does not perceive increase. Why is that?
Because internal emptiness does not exist and is not apprehended within the intrinsic nature of internal emptiness.
One does not perceive the arising of external emptiness;

one does not perceive its cessation, nor its grasping, nor its relinquishing; one does not perceive defilement, nor purification; one does not perceive accumulation, nor diminution; one does not perceive decrease, nor increase. Why is that?
For in this way, external emptiness does not exist and is not apprehended in the intrinsic nature of external emptiness;
one does not see the arising of internal-external emptiness,
nor does one see its cessation, nor does one see its grasping, nor does one see its relinquishing, nor does one see its affliction, nor does one see its purification.
He perceives neither accumulation nor depletion; he perceives neither decrease nor increase. Why is that?
Because internal-external emptiness does not exist and is not apprehended within the intrinsic nature of internal-external emptiness;
he does not perceive the arising of the emptiness of emptiness.

He does not perceive cessation, he does not perceive grasping, he does not perceive relinquishment, he does not perceive affliction, he does not perceive purification, he does not perceive accumulation, he does not perceive diminution, he does not perceive decrease, and he does not perceive increase. Why is that?
Because emptiness-emptiness does not exist and is not apprehended within the intrinsic nature of emptiness-emptiness.

One does not perceive the arising of great emptiness, nor does one perceive its cessation; one does not perceive grasping, nor does one perceive relinquishing; one does not perceive affliction, nor does one perceive purification; one does not perceive accumulation, nor does one perceive diminution; one does not perceive decrease, nor does one perceive increase. Why is that?
For thus, great emptiness does not exist and is not apprehended in the intrinsic nature of great emptiness;
one does not perceive the arising of ultimate emptiness, nor its cessation, nor its grasping.

He does not perceive relinquishment; he does not perceive affliction; he does not perceive purification; he does not perceive accumulation; he does not perceive diminution; he does not perceive decrease; he does not perceive increase. Why is that?
Because ultimate emptiness does not exist and is not apprehended within the intrinsic nature of ultimate emptiness.

One does not perceive the arising of conditioned emptiness, nor does one perceive its cessation; one does not perceive grasping, nor does one perceive relinquishing; one does not perceive affliction, nor does one perceive purification; one does not perceive accumulation, nor does one perceive diminution; one does not perceive decrease, nor does one perceive increase. Why is that?
For thus, conditioned emptiness does not exist and is not apprehended in the intrinsic nature of conditioned emptiness;
one does not perceive the arising of unconditioned emptiness, nor its cessation, nor its grasping, nor its relinquishing, nor its defilement, nor its purification.
He perceives neither accumulation nor diminution; he perceives neither loss nor increase. Why is that?
Because in the intrinsic nature of the emptiness of the unconditioned, the emptiness of the unconditioned, nothing exists and nothing is apprehended;
he does not perceive the arising of absolute emptiness.

He does not perceive cessation, he does not perceive grasping, he does not perceive relinquishment, he does not perceive affliction, he does not perceive purification, he does not perceive accumulation, he does not perceive diminution, he does not perceive decrease, and he does not perceive increase. Why is that?
Because absolute emptiness, in its very nature as absolute emptiness, neither exists nor is perceived.
One does not perceive the arising of the emptiness that is without beginning or end;

one does not perceive its cessation, nor its grasping, nor its relinquishing; one does not perceive its defilement, nor its purification; one does not perceive its accumulation, nor its diminution; one does not perceive its decrease, nor its increase. Why is that?
For thus, beginningless-and-endless emptiness does not exist and is not apprehended in the intrinsic nature of beginningless-and-endless emptiness;
one does not perceive the arising of the emptiness of non-dispersal,
nor does one perceive its cessation, nor does one perceive its grasping, nor does one perceive its relinquishment, nor does one perceive its affliction, nor does one perceive its purification.
He perceives neither accumulation nor depletion; he perceives neither loss nor increase. Why is that?
Because non-repudiation emptiness does not exist and is not apprehended within the intrinsic nature of non-repudiation emptiness;
he does not perceive the arising of natural emptiness.

One does not perceive cessation, one does not perceive grasping, one does not perceive relinquishment, one does not perceive affliction, one does not perceive purification, one does not perceive accumulation, one does not perceive diminution, one does not perceive decrease, and one does not perceive increase. Why is that?
Because intrinsic emptiness does not exist and is not apprehended within the intrinsic nature of intrinsic emptiness.
One does not perceive the arising of the emptiness of all phenomena;

one does not perceive their cessation, nor their grasping, nor their relinquishing; one does not perceive defilement, nor purification; one does not perceive accumulation, nor diminution; one does not perceive decrease, nor increase. Why is that?
For thus, the emptiness of all phenomena does not exist and is not apprehended within the intrinsic nature of the emptiness of all phenomena;
one does not perceive the arising of the emptiness of specific characteristics, nor does one perceive its cessation, nor its grasping, nor its relinquishing, nor its defilement, nor its purification.
He perceives neither accumulation nor diminution; he perceives neither loss nor increase. Why is that?
Because the emptiness of specific characteristics does not exist and is not apprehended within the intrinsic nature of the emptiness of specific characteristics;
nor does he perceive the arising of the emptiness of non-apprehension.

He does not perceive cessation, he does not perceive grasping, he does not perceive relinquishment, he does not perceive affliction, he does not perceive purification, he does not perceive accumulation, he does not perceive diminution, he does not perceive decrease, and he does not perceive increase. Why is that?
Because non-apprehension-emptiness, being of the nature of non-apprehension-emptiness, neither exists nor is apprehended.

One does not perceive the arising of the emptiness of non-existence, nor does one perceive its cessation; one does not perceive grasping, nor does one perceive relinquishing; one does not perceive affliction, nor does one perceive purification;
one does not perceive accumulation, nor does one perceive diminution; one does not perceive decrease, nor does one perceive increase. Why is that?
For thus, non-existence-emptiness and existence-emptiness do not exist and are not apprehended in the intrinsic nature;
one does not perceive the arising of intrinsic-nature-emptiness, nor its cessation, nor its grasping, nor its relinquishing, nor its affliction, nor its purification.
He perceives neither accumulation nor diminution; he perceives neither loss nor increase. Why is that?
Because intrinsic emptiness does not exist and is not apprehended within the nature of intrinsic emptiness;
he does not perceive the arising of the emptiness of the nature of non-existence.

He does not perceive cessation, he does not perceive grasping, he does not perceive relinquishment, he does not perceive affliction, he does not perceive purification, he does not perceive accumulation, he does not perceive diminution, he does not perceive decrease, and he does not perceive increase. Why is that?
Because suchness—the emptiness of intrinsic nature and the emptiness of non-existence—is neither found nor perceived within the intrinsic nature of the emptiness of intrinsic nature.

One does not perceive the arising of the applications of mindfulness, nor does one perceive their cessation; one does not perceive grasping, nor does one perceive relinquishing; one does not perceive affliction, nor does one perceive purification;
one does not perceive accumulation, nor does one perceive diminution; one does not perceive decrease, nor does one perceive increase. Why is that?
For in this way, the foundations of mindfulness do not exist and are not apprehended within the intrinsic nature of the foundations of mindfulness;
nor does one perceive the arising of the right efforts.
He does not perceive cessation, nor does he perceive grasping, nor does he perceive relinquishment; he does not perceive affliction, nor does he perceive purification;
he does not perceive accumulation, nor does he perceive diminution; he does not perceive decrease, nor does he perceive increase. Why is that?
Because the right efforts do not exist and are not apprehended within the intrinsic nature of the right efforts.

He perceives the arising of the bases of psychic power, yet he does not perceive their cessation; he does not perceive grasping, nor does he perceive relinquishing; he does not perceive affliction, nor does he perceive purification;
he does not perceive accumulation, nor does he perceive diminution; he does not perceive decrease, nor does he perceive increase. Why is that?
For in this way, the bases of psychic power do not exist and are not apprehended in their own-being as bases of psychic power; one does not see the arising of the faculties,
nor does one see their cessation, nor does one see their grasping, nor does one see their relinquishing, nor does one see their affliction, nor does one see their purification.
He perceives neither accumulation nor depletion; he perceives neither decrease nor increase. Why is that?
Because the faculties do not exist and are not apprehended within the intrinsic nature of the faculties;
he does not perceive the arising of the powers.

One does not perceive cessation, one does not perceive grasping, one does not perceive relinquishment, one does not perceive affliction, one does not perceive purification, one does not perceive accumulation, one does not perceive diminution, one does not perceive decrease, and one does not perceive increase. Why is that?
Because the powers do not exist and are not perceived within the intrinsic nature of the powers.

One does not see the arising of the factors of enlightenment, nor does one see their cessation; one does not see grasping, nor does one see relinquishing; one does not see affliction, nor does one see purification; one does not see accumulation, nor does one see diminution; one does not see decrease, nor does one see increase. Why is that?
For in this way, the factors of enlightenment do not exist and are not apprehended in the intrinsic nature of the factors of enlightenment;
one does not perceive the arising of the noble eightfold path, nor its cessation, nor its grasping, nor its relinquishing, nor its affliction, nor its purification.
He perceives neither increase nor decrease; he perceives neither loss nor growth. Why is that?
Because the path does not exist and is not apprehended within the intrinsic nature of the path;
he does not perceive the arising of the noble truths.

He does not perceive cessation, he does not perceive grasping, he does not perceive relinquishment, he does not perceive affliction, he does not perceive purification, he does not perceive accumulation, he does not perceive diminution, he does not perceive decrease, and he does not perceive increase. Why is that?
Because the noble truths do not exist and are not apprehended within the intrinsic nature of the noble truths.

One does not perceive the arising of the meditative absorptions, nor does one perceive their cessation; one does not perceive grasping, nor does one perceive relinquishing; one does not perceive affliction, nor does one perceive purification;
one does not perceive accumulation, nor does one perceive diminution; one does not perceive decrease, nor does one perceive increase. For what reason?
For in this way, the meditative absorptions do not exist and are not perceived within the intrinsic nature of meditative absorption;
one does not see the arising of the immeasurables,
nor does one see their cessation, nor does one see their grasping, nor does one see their relinquishing, nor does one see their defilement, nor does one see their purification.
He perceives neither accumulation nor diminution; he perceives neither loss nor increase. Why is that?
Because the immeasurables do not exist and are not apprehended within the nature of the immeasurable.
He does not perceive the arising of the formless attainments.

He does not perceive cessation, he does not perceive grasping, he does not perceive relinquishment, he does not perceive affliction, he does not perceive purification, he does not perceive accumulation, he does not perceive diminution, he does not perceive decrease, and he does not perceive increase. Why is that?
Because the formless attainments do not exist and are not apprehended within the intrinsic nature of the formless attainments.

He does not perceive the arising of the eight liberations; he does not perceive their cessation, nor does he perceive grasping, nor does he perceive relinquishing; he does not perceive affliction, nor does he perceive purification; he does not perceive accumulation, nor does he perceive diminution; he does not perceive decrease, nor does he perceive increase. Why is that?
For in this way, the liberations do not exist and are not apprehended in the intrinsic nature of liberation;
one does not perceive the arising of the serial attainments of meditative dwelling,
nor does one perceive their cessation, nor does one perceive grasping, nor does one perceive relinquishing, nor does one perceive affliction, nor does one perceive purification.
He perceives neither accumulation nor diminution; he perceives neither loss nor increase. Why is that?
Because the successive attainments of meditative dwelling do not exist and are not apprehended within the intrinsic nature of the successive attainments of meditative dwelling;
he does not perceive the arising of the gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness.

One does not perceive cessation, nor does one perceive grasping, nor does one perceive relinquishment; one does not perceive affliction, nor does one perceive purification; one does not perceive accumulation, nor does one perceive diminution; one does not perceive decrease, nor does one perceive increase. Why is that?

Because the gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—do not exist and are not apprehended within the intrinsic nature of the gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness.

He does not perceive the arising of the superknowledges, nor does he perceive their cessation; he does not perceive grasping, nor does he perceive relinquishing; he does not perceive affliction, nor does he perceive purification;
he does not perceive accumulation, nor does he perceive diminution; he does not perceive decrease, nor does he perceive increase. That...
For what reason?
Because the supernormal knowledges do not exist and are not apprehended within the intrinsic nature of the supernormal knowledges;
one does not perceive the arising of the meditative concentrations.

He does not perceive cessation, he does not perceive grasping, he does not perceive relinquishment, he does not perceive affliction, he does not perceive purification, he does not perceive accumulation, he does not perceive diminution, he does not perceive decrease, and he does not perceive increase. Why is that?
Because, in the intrinsic nature of meditative concentration, concentrations do not exist and are not apprehended.

He does not perceive the arising of the gateways of dhāraṇī, nor does he perceive their cessation; he does not perceive grasping, nor does he perceive relinquishing; he does not perceive affliction, nor does he perceive purification;
he does not perceive accumulation, nor does he perceive diminution; he does not perceive decrease, nor does he perceive increase. Why is that?
For in this way, the gateways of dhāraṇī do not exist and are not apprehended within the intrinsic nature of the gateways of dhāraṇī;
one does not see the arising of the powers of a Tathāgata,
nor does one see their cessation, nor does one see grasping, nor does one see relinquishing, nor does one see affliction, nor does one see purification.
He perceives neither accumulation nor diminution; he perceives neither loss nor increase. Why is that?
Because the powers of a Tathāgata do not exist and are not apprehended within the intrinsic nature of the powers of a Tathāgata;
he does not perceive the arising of the grounds of self-confidence.

He does not perceive cessation, he does not perceive grasping, he does not perceive relinquishment, he does not perceive affliction, he does not perceive purification, he does not perceive accumulation, he does not perceive diminution, he does not perceive decrease, and he does not perceive increase. Why is that?
Because, in the intrinsic nature of the fearlessnesses, the fearlessnesses do not exist and are not apprehended.

He does not perceive the arising of the analytical knowledges, nor does he perceive their cessation; he does not perceive grasping, nor does he perceive relinquishing; he does not perceive affliction, nor does he perceive purification;
he does not perceive accumulation, nor does he perceive diminution; he does not perceive decrease, nor does he perceive increase. For what reason?
For thus, the analytical knowledges do not exist and are not apprehended in the intrinsic nature of the analytical knowledges;
one does not perceive the arising of great loving-kindness,
nor does one perceive its cessation, nor does one perceive its grasping, nor does one perceive its relinquishing, nor does one perceive its affliction, nor does one perceive its purification.
He perceives neither accumulation nor diminution; he perceives neither loss nor increase. Why is that?
Because great loving-kindness does not exist and is not apprehended within the intrinsic nature of great loving-kindness;
he does not perceive the arising of great compassion.

One does not perceive cessation, nor does one perceive grasping, nor does one perceive relinquishment; one does not perceive affliction, nor does one perceive purification; one does not perceive accumulation, nor does one perceive diminution; one does not perceive decrease, nor does one perceive increase. For what reason?
For in this way, great compassion does not exist and is not apprehended within the intrinsic nature of great compassion;

it does not perceive the arising of the unique qualities of a Buddha (āveṇikabuddhadharma), nor does it perceive their cessation; it does not perceive grasping, nor does it perceive relinquishing; it does not perceive affliction, nor does it perceive purification.
He perceives neither accumulation nor diminution; he perceives neither loss nor increase. Why is that?
Because the unique qualities of a Buddha (āveṇikabuddhadharma) do not exist and are not apprehended within the intrinsic nature of the unique qualities of a Buddha;
he does not perceive the arising of omniscience.
He does not perceive cessation, nor does he perceive grasping, nor does he perceive relinquishment; he does not perceive affliction, nor does he perceive purification;
he does not perceive accumulation, nor does he perceive diminution; he does not perceive decrease, nor does he perceive increase. Why is that?
Because omniscience, in its own-being as omniscience, neither exists nor is it apprehended.
One does not perceive the arising of the knowledge of the aspects of the path;

one does not perceive its cessation, nor its grasping, nor its relinquishing; one does not perceive its defilement, nor its purification; one does not perceive its accumulation, nor its diminution; one does not perceive its decrease, nor its increase. For what reason?
For in this way, the knowledge of the aspects of the path does not exist and is not apprehended within the intrinsic nature of the knowledge of the aspects of the path;

it does not perceive the arising of the knowledge of all aspects, nor does it perceive its cessation, nor does it perceive grasping, nor does it perceive relinquishing, nor does it perceive affliction, nor does it perceive purification.
He perceives neither accumulation nor diminution; he perceives neither loss nor increase. Why is that?
Because omniscience (*sarvākārajñatā*) does not exist and is not apprehended within the intrinsic nature of omniscience itself.

In this way, O Venerable Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva [perceives] for the sake of the non-arising and non-ceasing, the non-grasping and non-rejection, the non-defilement and non-purification, and the non-accumulation, non-diminution, and non-loss of all phenomena.
"By training in the perfection of wisdom for the sake of non-increase, one will emerge into all-aspect omniscience through the yoga of non-training and non-emergence.
Then Śakra, lord of the gods, said this to the venerable Śāradvatīputra:
"Venerable Śāradvatīputra, from where should the perfection of wisdom of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, be sought?"
Śāradvatīputra said:
“Devendra, the perfection of wisdom of the bodhisattvas, mahāsattvas, is to be sought in the Subhūti chapter.
Then Śakra, lord of the gods, addressed the venerable Subhūti as follows:
"Venerable Subhūti, this is your power, this is your sustaining grace, that the noble Śāradvatīputra has spoken thus:
'The perfection of wisdom of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, should be sought in the Subhūti-parivarta.'"
Subhūti said:
"Kauśika, this is not my power; this is not my empowerment.
Śakra asked: "Then, Venerable Subhūti, whose power is this? Whose empowerment is this?"
Subhūti said:
"Kauśika, this is the power of the Tathāgata; this is the sustaining grace of the Tathāgata.
Śakra said: "Venerable Subhūti, since all dharmas are without a basis, how can you speak in such a way?"
This is the power of the Tathāgata, this is the sustaining grace of the Tathāgata;
yet herein the Tathāgata is not perceived in the state of dharmatā which is without a basis, nor is the Tathāgata perceived in the Tathāgata.
Subhūti said:
"So it is, Kauśika, so it is. Apart from the nature of phenomena that is without a basis, a Tathāgata is not to be found."
