Just as, Kauśika, the measure of space cannot be apprehended, even so, Kauśika, the measure of the mind cannot be apprehended;
through the immeasurability of space comes the immeasurability of the mind, and through the immeasurability of the mind comes the immeasurability of the perfection of wisdom.
Because form is immeasurable, Kauśika, this perfection is immeasurable for bodhisattvas, mahāsattvas. For what reason?
Because, Kauśika, no measure of form is apprehended; just as, Kauśika, no measure of space is apprehended.
In the same way, Kauśika, no measure of form is apprehended;

because space is immeasurable, form is immeasurable, and because form is immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom is immeasurable. Because sound is immeasurable, Kauśika, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, is immeasurable. For what reason?
For in this way, Kauśika, no measure of sound is apprehended;
just as, Kauśika, no measure of space is apprehended,
even so, Kauśika, no measure of sound is apprehended.
Because space is immeasurable, sound is immeasurable; because sound is immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom is immeasurable.
Because fragrance is immeasurable, Kauśika, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, is immeasurable. Why is that?
Because, Kauśika, no measure of fragrance is apprehended.
Just as, Kauśika, the measure of space cannot be apprehended,
even so, Kauśika, the measure of fragrance cannot be apprehended;
through the immeasurability of space, there is the immeasurability of fragrance, and through the immeasurability of fragrance, there is the immeasurability of the perfection of wisdom.
Kauśika, because taste is immeasurable, this perfection is immeasurable for bodhisattva mahāsattvas. Why is that?
Because, Kauśika, no measure of taste is apprehended;
just as, Kauśika, no measure of space is apprehended.
In the same way, Kauśika, no measure of taste is apprehended;
because space is immeasurable, taste is immeasurable, and because taste is immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom is immeasurable.
Because touch is immeasurable, Kauśika, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, is immeasurable. For what reason?
For in this way, Kauśika, no measure of contact is apprehended;
just as, Kauśika, no measure of space is apprehended.
In the same way, Kauśika, no measure of contact is apprehended;

because space is immeasurable, contact is immeasurable, and because contact is immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom is immeasurable. Because phenomena are immeasurable, Kauśika, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, is immeasurable. For what reason?
For in this way, Kauśika, no measure of phenomena is apprehended; just as, Kauśika, no measure of space is apprehended,
even so, Kauśika, no measure of phenomena is apprehended.

Because space is immeasurable, phenomena are immeasurable; because phenomena are immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom is immeasurable. Because visual consciousness is immeasurable, Kauśika, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, is immeasurable. Why is that?
Because, Kauśika, no measure of visual consciousness is apprehended.
Just as, Kauśika, the measure of space cannot be apprehended, even so, Kauśika, the measure of visual consciousness cannot be apprehended.

Due to the immeasurability of space, there is the immeasurability of visual consciousness; due to the immeasurability of visual consciousness, there is the immeasurability of the perfection of wisdom.
Kauśika, because auditory consciousness is immeasurable, this perfection is immeasurable for bodhisattva mahāsattvas. Why is that?
Because, Kauśika, no measure of auditory consciousness is apprehended;
just as, Kauśika, no measure of space is apprehended.
In the same way, Kauśika, no measure of auditory consciousness is apprehended;
because space is immeasurable, auditory consciousness is immeasurable, and because auditory consciousness is immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom is immeasurable.
Because olfactory consciousness is immeasurable, Kauśika, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, is immeasurable. For what reason?
For in this way, Kauśika, no measure of olfactory consciousness is apprehended;
just as, Kauśika, no measure of space is apprehended,
even so, Kauśika, no measure of olfactory consciousness is apprehended.
Because space is immeasurable, nose-consciousness is immeasurable; because nose-consciousness is immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom is immeasurable.
Because tongue-consciousness is immeasurable, Kauśika, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, is immeasurable. For what reason?
Because, Kauśika, no measure of tongue-consciousness is apprehended.
Just as, Kauśika, the measure of space cannot be apprehended,
even so, Kauśika, the measure of tongue-consciousness cannot be apprehended;

through the immeasurability of space, there is the immeasurability of tongue-consciousness, and through the immeasurability of tongue-consciousness, there is the immeasurability of the perfection of wisdom.
Kauśika, because body-consciousness is immeasurable, this perfection is immeasurable for the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas. For what reason?
Because, Kauśika, no measure of body-consciousness is apprehended;
just as, Kauśika, no measure of space is apprehended.
In the same way, Kauśika, no measure of body-consciousness is apprehended;
because space is immeasurable, body-consciousness is immeasurable,
and because body-consciousness is immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom is immeasurable.
Kauśika, because mental consciousness is immeasurable, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, is immeasurable. Why is that?
Because, Kauśika, no measure of mental consciousness is apprehended;
just as, Kauśika, no measure of space is apprehended.
In the same way, Kauśika, no measure of mental consciousness is apprehended;

because space is immeasurable, mental consciousness is immeasurable, and because mental consciousness is immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom is immeasurable. Because visual contact is immeasurable, Kauśika, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, is immeasurable. For what reason is that?
For in this way, Kauśika, no measure of eye-contact is apprehended; just as, Kauśika, no measure of space is apprehended,
even so, Kauśika, no measure of eye-contact is apprehended.
Because space is immeasurable, eye-contact is immeasurable; because eye-contact is immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom is immeasurable.
Because ear-contact is immeasurable, Kauśika, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, is immeasurable. Why is that?
Because, Kauśika, no measure of ear-contact is apprehended.
Just as, Kauśika, the measure of space is not apprehended,
even so, Kauśika, the measure of ear-contact is not apprehended;
because space is immeasurable, ear-contact is immeasurable, and because ear-contact is immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom is immeasurable.
Kauśika, because olfactory contact is immeasurable, this perfection is immeasurable for bodhisattva mahāsattvas. For what reason?
Because, Kauśika, no measure of olfactory contact is apprehended;
just as, Kauśika, no measure of space is apprehended.
In the same way, Kauśika, no measure of olfactory contact is apprehended;

because space is immeasurable, olfactory contact is immeasurable, and because olfactory contact is immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom is immeasurable. Because gustatory contact is immeasurable, Kauśika, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, is immeasurable. For what reason?
For in this way, Kauśika, no measure of tongue-contact is apprehended; just as, Kauśika, no measure of space is apprehended,
even so, Kauśika, no measure of tongue-contact is apprehended.
Due to the immeasurability of space, there is the immeasurability of tongue-contact; due to the immeasurability of tongue-contact, there is the immeasurability of the perfection of wisdom.
Due to the measurelessness of body-contact, Kauśika, this perfection of the bodhisattva mahāsattvas is measureless. Why is that?
Because, Kauśika, no measure of body-contact is apprehended.
Just as, Kauśika, the measure of space cannot be apprehended,
even so, Kauśika, the measure of bodily contact cannot be apprehended;
through the immeasurability of space, there is the immeasurability of bodily contact, and through the immeasurability of bodily contact, [there is the immeasurability of the perfection of wisdom].
The immeasurability of the perfection of wisdom, Kauśika, is due to the immeasurability of mental contact; this is the immeasurable perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas. For what reason?
Because, Kauśika, no measure of mental contact is apprehended.
Just as, Kauśika, the measure of space cannot be apprehended,

even so, Kauśika, the measure of mental contact cannot be apprehended; through the immeasurability of space, there is the immeasurability of mental contact, and through the immeasurability of mental contact, there is the immeasurability of the perfection of wisdom.
Kauśika, because the sensation conditioned by eye-contact is immeasurable, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, is immeasurable. For what reason?
Because, Kauśika, no measure of the sensation conditioned by eye-contact is apprehended;
just as, Kauśika, no measure of space is apprehended.
In the same way, Kauśika, no measure for the feeling conditioned by eye-contact is apprehended;

because space is immeasurable, the feeling conditioned by eye-contact is immeasurable, and because the feeling conditioned by eye-contact is immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom is immeasurable. Because the feeling conditioned by ear-contact is immeasurable, Kauśika, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, is immeasurable. Why is that?
For in this way, Kauśika, no measure of the feeling conditioned by auditory contact is apprehended;
just as, Kauśika, no measure of space is apprehended,
even so, Kauśika, no measure of the feeling conditioned by auditory contact is apprehended.

Because space is immeasurable, the feeling conditioned by ear-contact is immeasurable; because the feeling conditioned by ear-contact is immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom is immeasurable. Because the feeling conditioned by nose-contact is immeasurable, Kauśika, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, is immeasurable. For what reason?
Because, Kauśika, no measure of the feeling conditioned by nose-contact is apprehended.
Just as, Kauśika, the measure of space cannot be apprehended, even so, Kauśika, the measure of the feeling conditioned by nose-contact cannot be apprehended.

Due to the immeasurability of space, there is the immeasurability of the feeling conditioned by nose-contact; due to the immeasurability of the feeling conditioned by nose-contact, there is the immeasurability of the perfection of wisdom.
Kauśika, because the sensation conditioned by tongue-contact is immeasurable, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, is immeasurable. Why is that?
Because, Kauśika, no measure of the sensation conditioned by tongue-contact is apprehended;
just as, Kauśika, no measure of space is apprehended.
In the same way, Kauśika, no measure of the feeling conditioned by tongue-contact is apprehended;

because space is immeasurable, the feeling conditioned by tongue-contact is immeasurable, and because the feeling conditioned by tongue-contact is immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom is immeasurable.
[The same applies to] the feeling conditioned by body-contact.
Kauśika, this perfection is immeasurable for bodhisattva mahāsattvas. Why is that?
Because, Kauśika, no measure of the feeling conditioned by bodily contact is apprehended;
just as, Kauśika, no measure of space is apprehended.
In the same way, Kauśika, no measure of the feeling conditioned by bodily contact is apprehended;

because space is immeasurable, the feeling conditioned by bodily contact is immeasurable, and because the feeling conditioned by bodily contact is immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom is immeasurable. Because the feeling conditioned by mental contact is immeasurable, Kauśika, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, is immeasurable. For what reason?
For in this way, Kauśika, no measure of the feeling conditioned by eye-contact is apprehended;
just as, Kauśika, no measure of space is apprehended,
even so, Kauśika, no measure of the feeling conditioned by eye-contact is apprehended.
Because space is immeasurable, the sensation conditioned by eye-contact is immeasurable; because the sensation conditioned by eye-contact is immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom is immeasurable.
Because the earth element is infinite, Kauśika, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, is infinite. Why is that?
Because, Kauśika, no measure of the earth element can be apprehended.
Just as, Kauśika, the measure of space cannot be apprehended,
even so, Kauśika, the measure of the earth element cannot be apprehended;

through the immeasurability of space, there is the immeasurability of the earth element, and through the immeasurability of the earth element, there is the immeasurability of the perfection of wisdom.
Kauśika, because the water element is immeasurable, this perfection is immeasurable for the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas. For what reason?
Because, Kauśika, no measure of the water element is apprehended;
just as, Kauśika, no measure of space is apprehended.

In the same way, Kauśika, no measure of the water element is apprehended; because space is immeasurable, the water element is immeasurable, and because the water element is immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom is immeasurable.
Because the fire element is immeasurable, Kauśika, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, is immeasurable. For what reason?
For thus, Kauśika, the measure of the element of fire is not apprehended;
just as, Kauśika, the measure of space is not apprehended,
even so, Kauśika, the measure of the element of fire is not apprehended.
Because space is immeasurable, the fire element is immeasurable; because the fire element is immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom is immeasurable.
Because the wind element is immeasurable, Kauśika, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, is immeasurable. For what reason?
Because, Kauśika, no measure of the wind element is apprehended.
Just as, Kauśika, the measure of space cannot be apprehended,

even so, Kauśika, the measure of the wind element cannot be apprehended; through the immeasurability of space, there is the immeasurability of the wind element, and through the immeasurability of the wind element, there is the immeasurability of the perfection of wisdom.
"Kauśika, because the element of space is immeasurable, this perfection is immeasurable for the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas. For what reason?
Because, Kauśika, no measure of the element of space can be apprehended."
Just as, Kauśika, the measure of space cannot be apprehended, even so, Kauśika, the measure of the element of space cannot be apprehended;

through the immeasurability of space, there is the immeasurability of the element of space, and through the immeasurability of the element of space, there is the immeasurability of the perfection of wisdom.
Kauśika, because the element of consciousness is immeasurable, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, is immeasurable. For what reason?
Because, Kauśika, no measure of the element of consciousness is apprehended;
just as, Kauśika, no measure of space is apprehended.
In the same way, Kauśika, no measure of the element of consciousness (vijñānadhātu) is apprehended;

because space is immeasurable, the element of consciousness is immeasurable, and because the element of consciousness is immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā) is immeasurable. Because ignorance (avidyā) is immeasurable, Kauśika, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the great beings, is immeasurable. For what reason?
For in this way, Kauśika, no measure of ignorance is apprehended;
just as, Kauśika, no measure of space is apprehended, even so, Kauśika, no measure of ignorance is apprehended.
Because space is immeasurable, ignorance is immeasurable; because ignorance is immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom is immeasurable.
Because conditioned phenomena (*saṃskāra*) are measureless, Kauśika, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, is measureless. For what reason?
Because, Kauśika, no measure of conditioned phenomena is apprehended.
Just as, Kauśika, the measure of space cannot be apprehended, even so, Kauśika, the measure of conditioned phenomena (*saṃskāra*) cannot be apprehended.

Through the immeasurability of space, there is the immeasurability of conditioned phenomena; through the immeasurability of conditioned phenomena, there is the immeasurability of the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*).
Because consciousness is immeasurable, Kauśika, this perfection is an immeasurable perfection for bodhisattva mahāsattvas. For what reason?
Because, Kauśika, no measure of consciousness is apprehended;
just as, Kauśika, no measure of space is apprehended.
In the same way, Kauśika, no measure of consciousness is apprehended;
because space is immeasurable, consciousness is immeasurable, and because consciousness is immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom is immeasurable.
Because name-and-form (nāmarūpa) is immeasurable, Kauśika, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, is immeasurable. For what reason is that?
For in this way, Kauśika, no measure of name-and-form is apprehended; just as, Kauśika, no measure of space is apprehended,
even so, Kauśika, no measure of name-and-form is apprehended.
Because space is immeasurable, name-and-form is immeasurable; because name-and-form is immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom is immeasurable.
Because the six sense bases are measureless, Kauśika, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, is measureless. Why is that?
Because, Kauśika, no measure of the six sense bases is apprehended.
Just as, Kauśika, the measure of space cannot be apprehended,
even so, Kauśika, the measure of the six sense-bases cannot be apprehended, because space is immeasurable.
The immeasurability of the six sense bases constitutes the immeasurability of the perfection of wisdom through the immeasurability of the six sense bases.
Through the immeasurability of contact, Kauśika, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, is immeasurable. For what reason?
Because, Kauśika, no measure of contact is apprehended.
Just as, Kauśika, the measure of space cannot be apprehended,
even so, Kauśika, the measure of touch cannot be apprehended;
through the immeasurability of space comes the immeasurability of touch, and through the immeasurability of touch comes the immeasurability of the perfection of wisdom.
Kauśika, because feeling is immeasurable, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, is immeasurable. Why is that?
Because, Kauśika, no measure of feeling is apprehended;
just as, Kauśika, no measure of space is apprehended.
In the same way, Kauśika, no measure of feeling (vedanā) is apprehended;
because space is immeasurable, feeling is immeasurable, and because feeling is immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā) is immeasurable.
Because craving (tṛṣṇā) is immeasurable, Kauśika, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the great beings, is immeasurable. For what reason?
For in this way, Kauśika, no measure of craving is apprehended; just as, Kauśika, no measure of space is apprehended,
even so, Kauśika, no measure of craving is apprehended.
Because space is immeasurable, craving is immeasurable; because craving is immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom is immeasurable.
Because grasping is measureless, Kauśika, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, is measureless. Why is that?
Because, Kauśika, no measure of grasping is apprehended.
Just as, Kauśika, the measure of space cannot be apprehended, even so, Kauśika, the measure of appropriation cannot be apprehended;
through the immeasurability of space comes the immeasurability of appropriation, and through the immeasurability of appropriation comes the immeasurability of the perfection of wisdom.
Because existence is immeasurable, Kauśika, this perfection is an immeasurable perfection for bodhisattva mahāsattvas. For what reason?
Because, Kauśika, no measure of existence is apprehended;
just as, Kauśika, no measure of space is apprehended.

In the same way, Kauśika, no measure of existence (bhava) is apprehended; because space is immeasurable, existence is immeasurable; because existence is immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā) is immeasurable.
Because birth is immeasurable, Kauśika, this perfection of wisdom is immeasurable for the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas. For what reason?
For in this way, Kauśika, no measure of birth is apprehended;
just as, Kauśika, no measure of space is apprehended,
even so, Kauśika, no measure of birth is apprehended.
Through the immeasurability of space, there is the immeasurability of birth; through the immeasurability of birth, there is the immeasurability of the perfection of wisdom.
Through the measurelessness of old age and death, Kauśika, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, is measureless. For what reason?
Because, Kauśika, the measure of old age and death—
It is not apprehended;
just as, Kauśika, the measure of space is not apprehended,
even so, Kauśika, the measure of old age and death is not apprehended.
Because space is immeasurable, old age and death are immeasurable; because old age and death are immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom is immeasurable.
Because the perfection of generosity is immeasurable, Kauśika, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, is immeasurable. For what reason?
Because, Kauśika, no measure of the perfection of generosity can be apprehended.
Just as, Kauśika, the measure of space cannot be apprehended, even so, Kauśika, the measure of the perfection of generosity cannot be apprehended.
Because space is immeasurable, the perfection of generosity is immeasurable; because the perfection of generosity is immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom is immeasurable.
Kauśika, because the perfection of ethical discipline is immeasurable, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, is immeasurable. Why is that?
Because, Kauśika, no measure of the perfection of ethical discipline is apprehended;
just as, Kauśika, no measure of space is apprehended.
In the same way, Kauśika, no measure of the perfection of ethical discipline is apprehended;
because space is immeasurable, the perfection of ethical discipline is immeasurable, and because the perfection of ethical discipline is immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom is immeasurable.
Because the perfection of patience is immeasurable, Kauśika, this perfection of the bodhisattva mahāsattvas is immeasurable. For what reason?
For in this way, Kauśika, no measure of the perfection of patience is apprehended; just as, Kauśika, no measure of space is apprehended,
even so, Kauśika, no measure of the perfection of patience is apprehended.
Because space is immeasurable, the perfection of patience is immeasurable; because the perfection of patience is immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom is immeasurable.
Because the perfection of vigor is immeasurable, Kauśika, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, is immeasurable. Why is that?
Because, Kauśika, no measure of the perfection of vigor is apprehended.
Just as, Kauśika, the measure of space cannot be apprehended,
even so, Kauśika, the measure of the perfection of vigor cannot be apprehended;
because space is immeasurable, the perfection of vigor is immeasurable, and because the perfection of vigor is immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom is immeasurable.
Kauśika, because the perfection of meditation is immeasurable, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, is immeasurable. Why is that?
Because, Kauśika, no measure of the perfection of meditation is apprehended;
just as, Kauśika, no measure of space is apprehended.
In the same way, Kauśika, no measure of the perfection of meditation is apprehended;
because space is immeasurable, the perfection of meditation is immeasurable; because the perfection of meditation is immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom is immeasurable.
Because the perfection of wisdom is immeasurable, Kauśika, this is the immeasurable perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas. For what reason?
For in this way, Kauśika, no measure of the perfection of wisdom is apprehended; just as, Kauśika, no measure of space is apprehended,
even so, Kauśika, no measure of the perfection of wisdom is apprehended.

Through the immeasurability of space, there is the immeasurability of the perfection of wisdom; through the immeasurability of the perfection of wisdom, there is the immeasurability of the perfection of wisdom. Through the measurelessness of internal emptiness, Kauśika, this is the immeasurable perfection for the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas. Why is that?
Because, Kauśika, no measure of internal emptiness is apprehended.

Just as, Kauśika, the measure of space cannot be apprehended, even so, Kauśika, the measure of internal emptiness cannot be apprehended; because space is immeasurable, internal emptiness is immeasurable, and because internal emptiness is immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom is immeasurable.
Kauśika, because external emptiness is immeasurable, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, is immeasurable. Why is that?
Because, Kauśika, no measure of external emptiness is apprehended;
just as, Kauśika, no measure of space is apprehended.
In the same way, Kauśika, no measure of external emptiness is apprehended;
because space is immeasurable, external emptiness is immeasurable, and because external emptiness is immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom is immeasurable.
Because internal-and-external emptiness is immeasurable, Kauśika, this perfection of the immeasurable belongs to the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas. For what reason?
For in this way, Kauśika, no measure of internal-and-external emptiness is apprehended;
just as, Kauśika, no measure of space is apprehended,
even so, Kauśika, no measure of internal-and-external emptiness is apprehended.
Because space is immeasurable, internal-and-external emptiness is immeasurable; because internal-and-external emptiness is immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom is immeasurable.
Because the emptiness of emptiness is immeasurable, Kauśika, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, is immeasurable. Why is that?
Because, Kauśika, no measure of the emptiness of emptiness is apprehended.
Just as, Kauśika, the measure of space cannot be apprehended, even so, Kauśika, the measure of the emptiness of emptiness cannot be apprehended.
Because space is immeasurable, the emptiness of emptiness is immeasurable; because the emptiness of emptiness is immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom is immeasurable.
Kauśika, because great emptiness is immeasurable, this perfection is immeasurable for the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas. For what reason?
Because, Kauśika, no measure of great emptiness is apprehended; it is, Kauśika, just as if, for example, the measure of space were [unapprehendable].
It is not apprehended;
in the same way, Kauśika, the measure of great emptiness is not apprehended.
Because space is immeasurable, great emptiness is immeasurable; because great emptiness is immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom is immeasurable.
Kauśika, because ultimate emptiness is immeasurable, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, is immeasurable. For what reason?
Because, Kauśika, no measure of ultimate emptiness is apprehended;
just as, for example, Kauśika, no measure of space is apprehended.
In the same way, Kauśika, no measure of ultimate emptiness is apprehended;
because space is immeasurable, ultimate emptiness is immeasurable, and because ultimate emptiness is immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom is immeasurable.
Because conditioned emptiness is immeasurable, Kauśika, this is the immeasurable perfection for the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas. For what reason is that?
For in this way, Kauśika, no measure of the emptiness of the conditioned is apprehended; just as, Kauśika, no measure of space is apprehended,
even so, Kauśika, no measure of the emptiness of the conditioned is apprehended.
Because space is immeasurable, conditioned emptiness is immeasurable; because conditioned emptiness is immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom is immeasurable.
Because unconditioned emptiness is measureless, Kauśika, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, is measureless. For what reason?
Because, Kauśika, no measure of unconditioned emptiness is apprehended.
Just as, Kauśika, the measure of space cannot be apprehended, even so, Kauśika, the measure of the emptiness of the unconditioned cannot be apprehended.
Because space is immeasurable, the emptiness of the unconditioned is immeasurable; because the emptiness of the unconditioned is immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom is immeasurable.
Kauśika, because absolute emptiness is immeasurable, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, is immeasurable. For what reason?
Because, Kauśika, no measure of absolute emptiness is apprehended;
just as, Kauśika, no measure of space is apprehended.
In the same way, Kauśika, no measure of absolute emptiness is apprehended;
because space is immeasurable, absolute emptiness is immeasurable; and because absolute emptiness is immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom is immeasurable.
Because beginningless and endless emptiness is immeasurable, Kauśika, this is the immeasurable perfection for the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas. For what reason?
For in this way, Kauśika, no measure of the emptiness that is without beginning or end is apprehended;
just as, Kauśika, no measure of space is apprehended,
even so, Kauśika, no measure of the emptiness that is without beginning or end is apprehended.
Because space is immeasurable, beginningless and endless emptiness is immeasurable; because beginningless and endless emptiness is immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom is immeasurable.
Because non-repudiation emptiness is immeasurable, Kauśika, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, is immeasurable. For what reason?
Because, Kauśika, no measure of non-repudiation emptiness is apprehended.
Just as, Kauśika, the measure of space cannot be apprehended, even so, Kauśika, the measure of the emptiness of non-dispersal (anavakāra-śūnyatā) cannot be apprehended.

Through the immeasurability of space, there is the immeasurability of the emptiness of non-dispersal; through the immeasurability of the emptiness of non-dispersal, there is the immeasurability of the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā).
Kauśika, because intrinsic emptiness is immeasurable, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, is immeasurable. For what reason?
Because, Kauśika, no measure of intrinsic emptiness is apprehended;
just as, Kauśika, no measure of space is apprehended.
In the same way, Kauśika, no measure of the emptiness of intrinsic nature (prakṛti-śūnyatā) is apprehended;

because space is immeasurable, the emptiness of intrinsic nature is immeasurable; and because the emptiness of intrinsic nature is immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā) is immeasurable.
Because all dharmas are immeasurable in their emptiness, Kauśika, this perfection of wisdom of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, is immeasurable. For what reason?
For in this way, Kauśika, no measure of the emptiness of all dharmas is apprehended; just as, Kauśika, no measure of space is apprehended,
even so, Kauśika, no measure of the emptiness of all dharmas is apprehended.
Because space is immeasurable, the emptiness of all phenomena is immeasurable; because the emptiness of all phenomena is immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom is immeasurable.
Because the emptiness of specific characteristics is measureless, Kauśika, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, is measureless. Why is that?
Because, Kauśika, no measure for the emptiness of specific characteristics is apprehended.
Just as, Kauśika, the measure of space cannot be apprehended, even so, Kauśika, the measure of the emptiness of specific characteristics cannot be apprehended.

Through the immeasurability of space, there is the immeasurability of the emptiness of specific characteristics; through the immeasurability of the emptiness of specific characteristics, there is the immeasurability of the perfection of wisdom.
Kauśika, because non-apprehension and emptiness are immeasurable, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, is immeasurable. Why is that?
Because, Kauśika, no measure of non-apprehension and emptiness is apprehended;
it is just as, for example, Kauśika, no measure of space is apprehended.
In the same way, Kauśika, no measure of the emptiness of non-apprehension is apprehended;

because space is immeasurable, the emptiness of non-apprehension is immeasurable, and because the emptiness of non-apprehension is immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom is immeasurable. Because the emptiness of non-existence is immeasurable, Kauśika, this perfection of wisdom is immeasurable for the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas. For what reason?
For in this way, Kauśika, no measure of the emptiness of non-existence is apprehended;
just as, Kauśika, no measure of space is apprehended, even so, Kauśika, no measure of the emptiness of non-existence is apprehended. (ŚsP_II-3_200)
Because space is immeasurable, non-existence-emptiness is immeasurable; because non-existence-emptiness is immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom is immeasurable.
Because self-nature-emptiness is measureless, Kauśika, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, is measureless. Why is that?
Because, Kauśika, no measure of self-nature-emptiness is apprehended.
Just as, Kauśika, the measure of space cannot be apprehended, even so, Kauśika, the measure of the emptiness of intrinsic nature cannot be apprehended.
Because space is immeasurable, the emptiness of intrinsic nature is immeasurable; because the emptiness of intrinsic nature is immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom is immeasurable.
Kauśika, because the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence is immeasurable, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, is an immeasurable perfection. For what reason?
Because, Kauśika, no measure of the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence is apprehended;
just as, Kauśika, no measure of space is apprehended.
In the same way, Kauśika, no measure of the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence is apprehended;

because space is immeasurable, the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence is immeasurable; and because internal emptiness is immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom is immeasurable. Because the applications of mindfulness are immeasurable, Kauśika, this is the immeasurable perfection for the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas. For what reason?
For in this way, Kauśika, no measure of the applications of mindfulness is apprehended;
just as, Kauśika, no measure of space is apprehended,
even so, Kauśika, no measure of the applications of mindfulness is apprehended.
Because space is immeasurable, the applications of mindfulness are immeasurable; because the applications of mindfulness are immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom is immeasurable.
Because the right efforts are immeasurable, Kauśika, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, is immeasurable. For what reason?
Because, Kauśika, no measure of the right efforts is apprehended.
Just as, Kauśika, the measure of space cannot be apprehended, even so, Kauśika, the measure of the right efforts cannot be apprehended.
Due to the immeasurability of space, there is the immeasurability of the right efforts; due to the immeasurability of the right efforts, there is the immeasurability of the perfection of wisdom.
Kauśika, because the bases of psychic power are immeasurable, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, is immeasurable. For what reason?
Because, Kauśika, no measure of the bases of psychic power is apprehended; just as, Kauśika, no measure of space is apprehended.

In the same way, Kauśika, no measure of the bases of psychic power (*ṛddhipāda*) is apprehended; because space is immeasurable, the bases of psychic power are immeasurable, and because the bases of psychic power are immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*) is immeasurable.
Because the faculties (*indriya*) are immeasurable, Kauśika, this perfection of the bodhisattvas is immeasurable.
of the great beings. For what reason? Because, Kauśika, no measure of the faculties is apprehended;
just as, Kauśika, no measure of space is apprehended.
In the same way, Kauśika, no measure of the sense faculties is apprehended;

because space is immeasurable, the sense faculties are immeasurable; because the sense faculties are immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom is immeasurable. Because the powers are immeasurable, Kauśika, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, is immeasurable. For what reason?
For in this way, Kauśika, no measure of the powers is apprehended; just as, Kauśika, no measure of space is apprehended,
even so, Kauśika, no measure of the powers is apprehended.
Because space is immeasurable, power is immeasurable; because power is immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom is immeasurable.
Because the factors of enlightenment (bodhyaṅga) are immeasurable, Kauśika, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, is immeasurable. Why is that?
Because, Kauśika, no measure of the factors of enlightenment is apprehended.
Just as, Kauśika, the measure of space cannot be apprehended,

even so, Kauśika, the measure of the factors of enlightenment cannot be apprehended; because space is immeasurable, the factors of enlightenment are immeasurable, and because the factors of enlightenment are immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom is immeasurable.
Kauśika, because the noble eightfold path is immeasurable, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, is immeasurable. Why is that?
Because, Kauśika, no measure of the noble eightfold path is apprehended;
just as, Kauśika, no measure of space is apprehended.
In the same way, Kauśika, the measure of the noble eightfold path is not apprehended;
because space is immeasurable, the noble eightfold path is immeasurable; and because the noble eightfold path is immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom is immeasurable.
Because the noble truths are immeasurable, Kauśika, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, is immeasurable. For what reason?
For in this way, Kauśika, no measure of the noble truths is apprehended;
just as, Kauśika, no measure of space is apprehended,
even so, Kauśika, no measure of the noble truths is apprehended.
Because space is immeasurable, the noble truths are immeasurable; because the noble truths are immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom is immeasurable.
Because the meditative concentrations (*dhyāna*) are immeasurable, Kauśika, this perfection of the immeasurable belongs to the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas. For what reason?
Because, Kauśika, no measure of the meditative concentrations can be apprehended.
Just as, Kausika, the measure of space cannot be apprehended,
even so, Kausika, the measure of the meditative concentrations cannot be apprehended;
because space is immeasurable, the meditative concentrations are immeasurable, and because the meditative concentrations are immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom is immeasurable.
Because it is immeasurable and without measure, Kauśika, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, is immeasurable. For what reason?
Because, Kauśika, no measure of the immeasurables is apprehended;
just as, for example, Kauśika, no measure of space is apprehended.

In the same way, Kauśika, no measure of the immeasurable is apprehended; because space is immeasurable, there is the immeasurability and boundlessness of the immeasurable, and through that immeasurability and boundlessness of the immeasurable, there is the boundlessness of the perfection of wisdom.
Because the formless attainments are immeasurable, Kauśika, this is the immeasurable perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas. For what reason?
For in this way, Kauśika, no measure of the formless attainments is apprehended; just as, Kauśika, no measure of space is apprehended,
even so, Kauśika, no measure of the formless attainments is apprehended.
Because space is immeasurable, the formless attainments are immeasurable; because the formless attainments are immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom is immeasurable.
Because the eight liberations are immeasurable, Kauśika, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, is immeasurable. For what reason?
Because, Kauśika, no measure of the eight liberations is apprehended.
Just as, Kauśika, the measure of space cannot be apprehended, even so, Kauśika, the measure of the eight liberations cannot be apprehended;
because space is immeasurable, the liberations are immeasurable, and because the liberations are immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom is immeasurable.
Kauśika, because the meditative attainments of the successive dwellings are immeasurable, this perfection of the bodhisattva mahāsattvas is immeasurable. For what reason?
Because, Kauśika, no measure of the meditative attainments of the successive dwellings is apprehended;
just as, for example, Kauśika, no measure of space is apprehended.

In the same way, Kauśika, no measure of the successive meditative attainments (*anupūrvavihārasamāpatti*) is apprehended; because space is immeasurable, the successive meditative attainments are immeasurable; and because the successive meditative attainments are immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*) is immeasurable.

Because the gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—are immeasurable, Kauśika, this perfection of the immeasurable belongs to the bodhisattvas, the great beings. For what reason?

For in this way, Kauśika, no measure of the gateways to liberation— emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness— is apprehended; just as, Kauśika, no measure of space is apprehended, even so, Kauśika, no measure of the gateways to liberation— emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness— is apprehended.

Because space is immeasurable, the gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—are immeasurable; because the gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—are immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom is immeasurable.
Because the superknowledges are immeasurable, Kauśika, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, is immeasurable. Why is that?
Because, Kauśika, no measure of the superknowledges can be apprehended.
Just as, Kauśika, the measure of space cannot be apprehended, even so, Kauśika, the measure of the superknowledges cannot be apprehended;
because space is immeasurable, the superknowledges are immeasurable, and because the superknowledges are immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom is immeasurable.
Kauśika, because of the immeasurability of meditative concentrations, this perfection is immeasurable for bodhisattva mahāsattvas. For what reason?
Because, Kauśika, no measure of meditative concentrations is apprehended;
just as, Kauśika, no measure of space is apprehended.
In the same way, Kauśika, no measure of the concentrations can be apprehended;

because space is immeasurable, the concentrations are immeasurable; because the concentrations are immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom is immeasurable; and because the gateways of the dhāraṇīs are immeasurable, Kauśika, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, is immeasurable. For what reason?
For in this way, Kauśika, no measure of the gateways of dhāraṇī is apprehended; just as, Kauśika, no measure of space is apprehended,
even so, Kauśika, no measure of the gateways of dhāraṇī is apprehended.
Because space is immeasurable, the gateways of the dhāraṇīs are immeasurable; because the gateways of the dhāraṇīs are immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom is immeasurable.
Because the powers of the Tathāgata are immeasurable, Kauśika, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, is immeasurable. For what reason?
Because, Kauśika, no measure of the powers of the Tathāgata is apprehended.
Just as, Kauśika, the measure of space cannot be apprehended, even so, Kauśika, the measure of the powers of a Tathāgata cannot be apprehended.
Because space is immeasurable, the powers of a Tathāgata are immeasurable; because the powers of a Tathāgata are immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom is immeasurable.
Kauśika, because the fearlessnesses are immeasurable, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, is immeasurable. For what reason?
Because, Kauśika, no measure of the fearlessnesses is apprehended;
just as, Kauśika, no measure of space is apprehended.
In the same way, Kauśika, no measure of the fearlessnesses (vaiśāradya) is apprehended;

because space is immeasurable, the fearlessnesses are immeasurable, and because the fearlessnesses are immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā) is immeasurable. Because the analytical knowledges (pratisaṃvid) are immeasurable, Kauśika, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the great beings, is immeasurable. For what reason?
For in this way, Kauśika, no measure of the analytical knowledges (pratisaṃvid) is apprehended; just as, Kauśika, no measure of space is apprehended,
even so, Kauśika, no measure of the analytical knowledges is apprehended.
Because space is immeasurable, analytical knowledge is immeasurable; because analytical knowledge is immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom is immeasurable.
Because great loving-kindness is immeasurable, Kauśika, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, is immeasurable. Why is that?
Because, Kauśika, no measure of great loving-kindness is apprehended.
Just as, Kauśika, the measure of space cannot be apprehended,

even so, Kauśika, the measure of great loving-kindness (*mahāmaitrī*) cannot be apprehended; because space is immeasurable, great loving-kindness is immeasurable, and because great loving-kindness is immeasurable, [it is infinite].
The immeasurability of the perfection of wisdom, Kauśika, is due to the immeasurability of great compassion; this is the immeasurable perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas. For what reason?
Because, Kauśika, no measure of great compassion can be apprehended.
Just as, Kauśika, the measure of space cannot be apprehended, even so, Kauśika, the measure of great compassion cannot be apprehended.
Because space is immeasurable, great compassion is immeasurable; because great compassion is immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom is immeasurable.
Because of the immeasurability of sympathetic joy (*muditā*), Kauśika, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, is immeasurable. For what reason?
Because, Kauśika, no measure of sympathetic joy is apprehended;
just as, Kauśika, no measure of space is apprehended.
In the same way, Kauśika, no measure of sympathetic joy (muditā) can be apprehended;
because space is immeasurable, sympathetic joy is immeasurable; and because sympathetic joy is immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā) is immeasurable.
Because equanimity (upekṣā) is immeasurable, Kauśika, this is the immeasurable perfection for the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas. For what reason?
For in this way, Kauśika, no measure of equanimity is apprehended; just as, Kauśika, no measure of space is apprehended,
even so, Kauśika, no measure of equanimity is apprehended.
Through the immeasurability of space, there is the immeasurability of equanimity; through the immeasurability of equanimity, there is the immeasurability of the perfection of wisdom.
Because, Kauśika, the unique qualities of a Buddha (āveṇikabuddhadharma) are immeasurable, this perfection of the bodhisattva mahāsattvas is immeasurable. Why is that?
Because, Kauśika, no measure of the unique qualities of a Buddha can be apprehended.
Just as, Kauśika, the measure of space cannot be apprehended, even so, Kauśika, the measure of the unique qualities of a Buddha (āveṇikabuddhadharma) cannot be apprehended.
Because space is immeasurable, the unique qualities of a Buddha are immeasurable; because the unique qualities of a Buddha are immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā) is immeasurable.
Kauśika, because omniscience is immeasurable, this perfection is immeasurable for the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas. For what reason?
Because, Kauśika, no measure of omniscience is apprehended;
just as, Kauśika, no measure of space is apprehended.
In the same way, Kauśika, no measure of omniscience is apprehended;

because space is immeasurable, omniscience is immeasurable, and because omniscience is immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom is immeasurable. Because the knowledge of the aspects of the path is immeasurable, Kauśika, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, is immeasurable. For what reason?
For in this way, Kauśika, no measure of the knowledge of the aspects of the path is apprehended;
just as, Kauśika, no measure of space is apprehended, even so, Kauśika, no measure of the knowledge of the aspects of the path is apprehended.
It is not apprehended;
because space is immeasurable, the knowledge of the aspects of the path is immeasurable; because the knowledge of the aspects of the path is immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom is immeasurable.
Because the knowledge of all aspects is immeasurable, Kauśika, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, is immeasurable.
For what reason?
Because, Kauśika, no measure of the knowledge of all aspects (sarvākārajñatā) is apprehended;
just as, Kauśika, no measure of space is apprehended.

In the same way, Kauśika, no measure of all-aspect-knowledge (*sarvākārajñatā*) is apprehended; because space is immeasurable, all-aspect-knowledge is immeasurable, and because all-aspect-knowledge is immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*) is immeasurable.
By this method, Kauśika, this perfection of wisdom is an immeasurable perfection for the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas.
Because form is infinite, Kauśika, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, is infinite. For what reason?
Because, Kauśika, neither an end nor a middle of form is apprehended.
Because feeling is infinite, Kauśika, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, is infinite. For what reason?
For in this way, Kauśika, neither an end nor a middle of feeling (vedanā) is apprehended;

because perception (saṃjñā) is immeasurable, Kauśika, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, is infinite. Why is that? For in this way, Kauśika, neither an end nor a middle of perception is apprehended.
Because conditioned phenomena (*saṃskāra*) are infinite, Kauśika, this perfection is infinite for the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas. For what reason?
Because, Kauśika, neither an end nor a middle of conditioned phenomena is apprehended.
Because consciousness (*vijñāna*) is infinite, Kauśika, this perfection is infinite for the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas. For what reason?
For in this way, Kauśika, neither the end nor the middle of consciousness is apprehended.
Because the eye is infinite, Kauśika, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, is infinite. Why is that?
For in this way, Kauśika, neither the end nor the middle of the eye is apprehended.
Because the ear is infinite, Kauśika, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, is infinite. For what reason?
Because, Kauśika, neither an end nor a middle of the ear is apprehended.
Because the nose is infinite, Kauśika, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, is infinite. For what reason?
For in this way, Kauśika, neither an end nor a middle of the nose is apprehended;
because the tongue is infinite, Kauśika, this perfection is an infinite perfection for the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas. Why is that?
Because, Kauśika, neither an end nor a middle of the nose is apprehended.
“Kauśika, because the body is infinite, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, is infinite. For what reason?
Because, Kauśika, neither an end nor a middle of the body is apprehended.
Kauśika, because the mind is infinite, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, is infinite. For what reason?”
For in this way, Kauśika, neither the end nor the middle of the mind is apprehended.
Because form is infinite, Kauśika, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, is infinite. Why is that?
For in this way, Kauśika, neither the end nor the middle of form is apprehended;
because sound is infinite, Kauśika, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, is infinite. Why is that?
For in this way, Kauśika, neither the end nor the middle of sound is apprehended.
"Kauśika, because of the infinity of fragrance, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, is infinite. Why is that?
Because, Kauśika, neither an end nor a middle of fragrance can be apprehended.
Because of the infinity of taste, Kauśika, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, is infinite. Why is that?"
For in this way, Kauśika, neither an end nor a middle of taste is apprehended;
because of the infinitude of touch, Kauśika, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, is infinite. Why is that?
For in this way, Kauśika, neither an end nor a middle of touch is apprehended.
"Kauśika, because phenomena are infinite, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, is infinite. Why is that?
Because, Kauśika, neither an end nor a middle of phenomena is apprehended.
Because visual consciousness is infinite, Kauśika, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, is infinite. Why is that?"
For in this way, Kauśika, neither an end nor a middle of eye-consciousness is apprehended;
because of the infinity of ear-consciousness, Kauśika, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, is infinite. Why is that?
For in this way, Kauśika, neither an end nor a middle of ear-consciousness is apprehended.
Kauśika, because olfactory consciousness is infinite, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, is infinite. Why is that?
Because, Kauśika, neither an end nor a middle of olfactory consciousness is apprehended.
Because gustatory consciousness is infinite, Kauśika, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, is infinite. Why is that?
For in this way, Kauśika, neither an end nor a middle of tongue-consciousness is apprehended;
because body-consciousness is infinite, Kauśika, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, is infinite. Why is that?
For in this way, Kauśika, neither an end nor a middle of body-consciousness is apprehended.
Kauśika, because mental consciousness is infinite, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, is infinite. Why is that?
Because, Kauśika, neither an end nor a middle of mental consciousness is apprehended.
Because visual contact is infinite, Kauśika, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, is infinite. Why is that?
For in this way, Kauśika, neither an end nor a middle of visual contact is apprehended;
because of the infinity of auditory contact, Kauśika, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, is infinite. Why is that?
Because, Kauśika, neither an end nor a middle of auditory contact is apprehended.
Kauśika, because olfactory contact is infinite, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, is infinite.
For what reason?
Because, Kauśika, neither an end nor a middle of olfactory contact is apprehended.
Because of the infinity of tongue-contact, Kauśika, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, is infinite. For what reason?
Because, Kauśika, neither an end nor a middle of tongue-contact is apprehended.
Because of the infinity of body-contact, Kauśika, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, is infinite. For what reason?
For in this way, Kauśika, neither an end nor a middle of bodily contact is apprehended;
because of the infinity of mental contact, Kauśika, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, is infinite. Why is that?
Because, Kauśika, neither an end nor a middle of mental contact is apprehended.
"Kauśika, because the feeling conditioned by eye-contact is infinite, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, is infinite. Why is that?
Because, Kauśika, neither an end nor a middle of the feeling conditioned by eye-contact is apprehended.
Because the feeling conditioned by ear-contact is infinite, Kauśika, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, is infinite. Why is that?"
For in this way, Kauśika, neither an end nor a middle is perceived in the feeling conditioned by ear-contact;
because of the infinity of the feeling conditioned by nose-contact, Kauśika, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, is infinite. Why is that?
For in this way, Kauśika, neither an end nor a middle is perceived in the feeling conditioned by nose-contact.
Kauśika, because the sensation conditioned by tongue-contact is infinite, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, is infinite. Why is that?
Because, Kauśika, neither an end nor a middle is apprehended in the sensation conditioned by tongue-contact.
Kauśika, because the sensation conditioned by body-contact is infinite, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, is infinite. Why is that?
For in this way, Kauśika, neither an end nor a middle is perceived in the feeling conditioned by bodily contact;
because the feeling conditioned by mental contact is infinite, Kauśika, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, is infinite. Why is that?
For in this way, Kauśika, neither an end nor a middle is perceived in the feeling conditioned by visual contact.
"Kauśika, because the earth element is infinite, this perfection of the bodhisattva mahāsattvas is infinite. For what reason?
Because, Kauśika, no end of the earth element is apprehended;
just as, Kauśika, neither an end nor a middle of space is apprehended."
Because the water element is infinite, Kauśika, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, is infinite. For what reason?
Because, Kauśika, no end of the water element is apprehended;
just as, Kauśika, neither an end nor a middle of space is apprehended.
“Kauśika, because the fire element is infinite, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, is infinite. Why is that?
Because, Kauśika, neither an end nor a middle of the fire element is perceived.”
Because the wind element is infinite, Kauśika, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, is infinite. For what reason?
Because, Kauśika, neither an end nor a middle of the wind element is apprehended.
Because the space element is infinite, Kauśika, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, is infinite. For what reason?
For in this way, Kauśika, neither an end nor a middle of the space-element (ākāśadhātu) is apprehended;
because the consciousness-element (vijñānadhātu) is infinite, Kauśika, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, is infinite. Why is that?
Because, Kauśika, neither an end nor a middle of the consciousness-element is apprehended.
Because ignorance is infinite, Kauśika, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, is infinite. Why is that?
Because, Kauśika, neither an end nor a middle of ignorance is apprehended.
Because formative forces (*saṃskāra*) are infinite, Kauśika, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, is infinite. Why is that?
For in this way, Kauśika, neither the end nor the middle of conditioned phenomena (*saṃskāra*) is apprehended;
because consciousness (*vijñāna*) is infinite, Kauśika, this perfection (*pāramitā*) of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, is infinite. Why is that?
Because, Kauśika, neither the end nor the middle of consciousness is apprehended.
“Kauśika, because name-and-form (*nāmarūpa*) is infinite, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, is infinite. For what reason?
Because, Kauśika, neither an end nor a middle of name-and-form is perceived.
Because the six sense bases (*ṣaḍāyatana*) are infinite, Kauśika, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, is infinite. For what reason?”
For in this way, Kauśika, neither an end nor a middle of the six sense-bases (ṣaḍāyatana) is apprehended;
because contact (sparśa) is infinite, Kauśika, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, is infinite. Why is that?
For in this way, Kauśika, neither an end nor a middle of contact is apprehended.
Kauśika, because feeling is infinite, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, is infinite. For what reason?
Because, Kauśika, neither an end nor a middle of feeling can be apprehended.
Because craving is infinite, Kauśika, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, is infinite. For what reason?
For in this way, Kauśika, neither the end nor the middle of craving is apprehended;
because grasping is infinite, Kauśika, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, is infinite. Why is that?
Because, Kauśika, neither the end nor the middle of grasping is apprehended.
Because existence is infinite, Kauśika, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, is infinite. For what reason?
Because, Kauśika, neither an end nor a middle of existence is apprehended.
Because birth is infinite, Kauśika, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, is infinite. For what reason?
For in this way, Kauśika, neither an end nor a middle of birth is apprehended;
because old age and death are endless, Kauśika, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, is endless. Why is that?
For in this way, Kauśika, neither an end nor a middle of old age and death is apprehended.
Kauśika, because the perfection of generosity is infinite, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, is infinite. Why is that?
Because, Kauśika, neither an end nor a middle of the perfection of generosity can be apprehended.
Kauśika, because the perfection of ethical discipline is infinite, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, is infinite. Why is that?
Because, Kauśika, neither an end nor a middle of the perfection of ethical discipline can be apprehended.
Because the perfection of patience is infinite, Kauśika, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, is infinite. Why is that?
For in this way, Kauśika, neither an end nor a middle of the perfection of patience is apprehended;
and because of the infinity of the perfection of vigor, Kauśika, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, is infinite. Why is that?
For in this way, Kauśika, neither an end nor a middle of the perfection of vigor is apprehended.
"Kauśika, because the perfection of meditation is infinite, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, is infinite. For what reason?
Because, Kauśika, neither an end nor a middle of the perfection of meditation can be apprehended.
Kauśika, because the perfection of wisdom is infinite, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, is infinite. For what reason?"
For in this way, Kauśika, neither an end nor a middle of the perfection of wisdom is apprehended.
Because of the infinity of internal emptiness, Kauśika, this is an infinite perfection for the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas. Why is that?
For in this way, Kauśika, neither an end nor a middle of internal emptiness is apprehended.
Because of the infinitude of external emptiness (*bahirdhāśūnyatā*), Kauśika, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, is infinite. For what reason?
Because, Kauśika, in external emptiness neither an end nor a middle is apprehended.
Because of the infinitude of internal-and-external emptiness (*adhyātmabahirdhāśūnyatā*), Kauśika, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, is infinite. For what reason?
For in this way, Kauśika, neither an end nor a middle of internal-and-external emptiness is apprehended;
because of the infinity of the emptiness of emptiness, Kauśika, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, is infinite. Why is that?
For in this way, Kauśika, neither an end nor a middle of the emptiness of emptiness is apprehended.
Because of the infinity of great emptiness, Kauśika, this perfection is infinite for the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas. For what reason?
Because, Kauśika, in great emptiness neither an end nor a middle is perceived.
Because of the infinity of ultimate emptiness, Kauśika, this perfection is infinite for the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas. For what reason?
For in this way, Kauśika, neither an end nor a middle of ultimate emptiness (paramārtha-śūnyatā) is apprehended;
because of the infinity of conditioned emptiness (saṃskṛta-śūnyatā), Kauśika, this perfection is infinite for the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas. Why is that?
For in this way, Kauśika, neither an end nor a middle of conditioned emptiness is apprehended.
"Kauśika, because of the infinitude of the emptiness of the unconditioned (*asaṃskṛta-śūnyatā*), this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, is infinite. For what reason?
Because, Kauśika, in the emptiness of the unconditioned, neither an end nor a middle is perceived.
Because of the infinitude of the emptiness of the ultimate (*atyanta-śūnyatā*), Kauśika, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, is infinite. For what reason?"
For in this way, Kauśika, neither an end nor a middle is apprehended in absolute emptiness;
because of the endlessness of the emptiness of that which has no beginning or end, Kauśika, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, is endless. For what reason?
For in this way, Kauśika, neither an end nor a middle is perceived in the emptiness of that which has no beginning or end;
because of the infinity of the emptiness of non-dispersal, Kauśika, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, is infinite. Why is that?
For in this way, Kauśika, neither an end nor a middle is perceived in the emptiness of non-dispersal.
Kauśika, because the emptiness of intrinsic nature is infinite, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, is infinite. Why is that?
Because, Kauśika, in the emptiness of intrinsic nature, neither an end nor a middle is perceived.
Kauśika, because the emptiness of all phenomena is infinite, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, is infinite. Why is that?
For in this way, Kauśika, neither an end nor a middle of the emptiness of all dharmas is apprehended;
because of the infinity of the emptiness of intrinsic characteristics, Kauśika, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, is infinite. Why is that?
For in this way, Kauśika, neither an end nor a middle of the emptiness of intrinsic characteristics is apprehended.
Kauśika, because non-apprehension-emptiness is infinite, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, is infinite. For what reason?
Because, Kauśika, in non-apprehension-emptiness, neither an end nor a middle is apprehended.
Because non-existence-emptiness is infinite, Kauśika, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, is infinite. For what reason?
For in this way, Kauśika, neither an end nor a middle is apprehended in the emptiness of non-existence;
because of the infinity of the emptiness of intrinsic nature, Kauśika, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, is infinite. Why is that?
Because, Kauśika, neither an end nor a middle is apprehended in the emptiness of intrinsic nature.
"Kauśika, because the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence is infinite, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, is infinite. For what reason?
Because, Kauśika, in the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence, neither an end nor a middle is apprehended.
Because the applications of mindfulness are infinite, Kauśika, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, is infinite. For what reason?"
For it is thus, Kauśika: no end and no middle of the applications of mindfulness can be apprehended.
Because of the infinity of the right efforts, Kauśika, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, is infinite. Why is that?
For it is thus, Kauśika: no end and no middle of the right efforts can be apprehended.
Kauśika, because the bases of psychic power are infinite, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, is infinite. Why is that?
Because, Kauśika, neither an end nor a middle of the bases of psychic power is apprehended.
Kauśika, because the faculties are infinite, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, is infinite. Why is that?
For in this way, Kauśika, neither an end nor a middle of the faculties is apprehended;
because the powers are infinite, Kauśika, this perfection of the bodhisattva mahāsattvas is infinite. Why is that?
For in this way, Kauśika, there is neither an end nor [a middle] of the powers.
Neither a middle nor an end is perceived;
therefore, Kauśika, because the factors of enlightenment are infinite, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, is infinite. Why is that?
Because, Kauśika, neither an end nor a middle of the factors of enlightenment is perceived.
Because the noble eightfold path is infinite, Kauśika, this perfection of the bodhisattva mahāsattvas is infinite. For what reason?
Because, Kauśika, neither an end nor a middle of the noble eightfold path is apprehended.
Because the noble truths are infinite, Kauśika, this perfection of the bodhisattva mahāsattvas is infinite. For what reason?
For in this way, Kauśika, neither an end nor a middle of the noble truths is apprehended;
because of the infinity of the meditative absorptions, Kauśika, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, is infinite. Why is that?
Because, Kauśika, neither an end nor a middle of the meditative absorptions is apprehended.
“Kauśika, because they are immeasurable and infinite, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, is infinite. Why is that?
Because, Kauśika, for the immeasurables, neither an end nor a middle is perceived.
Because the formless attainments are infinite, Kauśika, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, is infinite. Why is that?”
For in this way, Kauśika, neither an end nor a middle of the formless attainments is apprehended;
because the eight liberations are infinite, Kauśika, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, is infinite. Why is that?
Because, Kauśika, neither an end nor a middle of the eight liberations is apprehended.
Kauśika, because the meditative attainments of the successive dwellings (*anupūrvavihārasamāpatti*) are infinite, this perfection of the bodhisattva mahāsattvas is infinite. For what reason?
Because, Kauśika, in the meditative attainments of the successive dwellings, neither an end nor a middle is apprehended.
Kauśika, because the gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—are infinite, this perfection of the bodhisattva mahāsattvas is immeasurable. For what reason?
For in this way, Kauśika, neither an end nor a middle is perceived among the gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness.
Because the supernormal powers are infinite, Kauśika, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, is infinite. Why is that?
Because, Kauśika, no end to the supernormal powers is perceived.
It is just as if, Kauśika, neither the end nor the middle of space can be apprehended;
because of the infinity of samādhi, Kauśika, this perfection of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, is infinite. For what reason?
