through the practice of neither grasping nor relinquishing olfactory contact.
By means of the yoga of non-appropriation and non-abandonment of tongue-contact,
by means of the yoga of non-appropriation and non-abandonment of body-contact, and by means of the yoga of non-appropriation and non-abandonment of mind-contact.

By means of the yoga of non-appropriation and non-abandonment of feeling conditioned by eye-contact; by means of the yoga of non-appropriation and non-abandonment of feeling conditioned by ear-contact;
by means of the yoga of non-appropriation and non-abandonment of feeling conditioned by nose-contact; [and so forth].
By means of the practice of neither grasping nor abandoning feeling conditioned by tongue-contact;
by means of the practice of neither grasping nor abandoning feeling conditioned by body-contact; and by means of the practice of neither grasping nor abandoning feeling conditioned by mind-contact.

By way of the non-appropriation and non-abandonment of the earth element, by way of the non-appropriation and non-abandonment of the water element, and by way of the non-appropriation and non-abandonment of the fire element.
by way of the non-appropriation and non-abandonment of the wind element, by way of the non-appropriation and non-abandonment of the space element,
and by way of the non-appropriation and non-abandonment of the consciousness element;

By means of the yoga of non-appropriation and non-abandonment of ignorance; by means of the yoga of non-appropriation and non-abandonment of formative predispositions; by means of the yoga of non-appropriation and non-abandonment of consciousness.
By means of the yoga of neither grasping nor abandoning name-and-form;
by means of the yoga of neither grasping nor abandoning the six sense bases; by means of the yoga of neither grasping nor abandoning contact;
by way of the yoga of non-appropriation and non-abandonment of sensation,
by way of the yoga of non-appropriation and non-abandonment of craving,
and by way of the yoga of non-appropriation and non-abandonment of clinging;
By means of the yoga of neither grasping nor abandoning existence;
by means of the yoga of neither grasping nor abandoning birth; and by means of the yoga of neither grasping nor abandoning old age and death.
by means of the yoga of non-appropriation and non-abandonment regarding the perfection of generosity;

by means of the yoga of non-appropriation and non-abandonment regarding the perfection of ethical discipline; and by means of the yoga of non-appropriation and non-abandonment regarding the perfection of patience.
By means of the yoga of non-appropriation and non-abandonment of the perfection of vigor;

by means of the yoga of non-appropriation and non-abandonment of the perfection of meditative concentration; and by means of the yoga of non-appropriation and non-abandonment of the perfection of wisdom.
by means of the yoga of non-appropriation and non-abandonment of internal emptiness, by means of the yoga of non-appropriation and non-abandonment of external emptiness,
and by means of the yoga of non-appropriation and non-abandonment of internal-and-external emptiness;
by means of the yoga of non-appropriation and non-abandonment of the emptiness of emptiness,
by means of the yoga of non-appropriation and non-abandonment of great emptiness, and by means of the yoga of non-appropriation and non-abandonment of the emptiness of the ultimate;
By means of the yoga of non-appropriation and non-abandonment of conditioned emptiness, by means of the yoga of non-appropriation and non-abandonment of unconditioned emptiness,
and by means of the yoga of non-appropriation and non-abandonment of absolute emptiness.
by means of the yoga of non-appropriation and non-abandonment of the emptiness of that which is without beginning or end,

by means of the yoga of non-appropriation and non-abandonment of the emptiness of non-dispersal, and by means of the yoga of non-appropriation and non-abandonment of the emptiness of intrinsic nature;

by means of the yoga of non-appropriation and non-abandonment of the emptiness of all phenomena, by means of the yoga of non-appropriation and non-abandonment of the emptiness of specific characteristics, and by means of the yoga of non-appropriation and non-abandonment of the emptiness of the unapprehendable;
By means of the yoga of non-appropriation and non-abandonment of the emptiness of non-existence;

by means of the yoga of non-appropriation and non-abandonment of the emptiness of intrinsic nature; and by means of the yoga of non-appropriation and non-abandonment of the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence.
by means of the yoga of non-appropriation and non-abandonment of the foundations of mindfulness;
by means of the yoga of non-appropriation and non-abandonment of the right efforts;
by means of the yoga of non-appropriation and non-abandonment of the bases of psychic power;

by means of the yoga of neither grasping nor abandoning the sense-faculties, by means of the yoga of neither grasping nor abandoning the powers, and by means of the yoga of neither grasping nor abandoning the factors of enlightenment;
by means of the practice of neither grasping nor abandoning the noble eightfold path;
by means of the practice of neither grasping nor abandoning the noble truths;
and by means of the practice of neither grasping nor abandoning the meditative absorptions.
by means of the yoga of non-appropriation and non-abandonment of the immeasurables;
by means of the yoga of non-appropriation and non-abandonment of the formless attainments; and by means of the yoga of non-appropriation and non-abandonment of the eight liberations.
By means of the yoga of non-appropriation and non-abandonment regarding the nine successive meditative attainments;
by means of the yoga of non-appropriation and non-abandonment regarding the gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness;
and by means of the yoga of non-appropriation and non-abandonment regarding the superknowledges.

by means of the yoga of non-appropriation and non-abandonment of the meditative concentrations; by means of the yoga of non-appropriation and non-abandonment of the gateways of dhāraṇīs; and by means of the yoga of non-appropriation and non-abandonment of the powers of a Tathāgata.
by means of the yoga of non-appropriation and non-abandonment of the grounds of self-confidence,
by means of the yoga of non-appropriation and non-abandonment of the analytical knowledges,
and by means of the yoga of non-appropriation and non-abandonment of great loving-kindness;
by means of the yoga of neither grasping nor abandoning the great compassions;
by means of the yoga of neither grasping nor abandoning the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha; and by means of the yoga of neither grasping nor abandoning all forms of omniscience.

by means of the yoga of non-appropriation and non-abandonment of the knowledge of the aspects of the path, and by means of the yoga of non-appropriation and non-abandonment of the knowledge of all aspects.
Then the Blessed One [addressed] the fourfold assembly— the monks, nuns, laymen, and laywomen— and the bodhisattvas, mahāsattvas.

And the sons of the gods belonging to the retinue of the Four Great Kings, the sons of the gods of the Thirty-three, the sons of the gods of the Yāma heaven, the sons of the gods of Tuṣita, the sons of the gods who Delight in Emanation, the sons of the gods who Wield Power over the Creations of Others,
the sons of the gods of the Brahma-realm, the sons of the gods who are Ministers of Brahmā, and the sons of the gods who are Retainers of Brahmā.
and the sons of gods who are Great Brahmās, the Ābhā deva-sons, the Parīttābhā deva-sons,
the Apramāṇābhā devas, the Ābhāsvara devas, the Śubha devas, the Parīttaśubha devas, the Pramāṇaśubha devas, the Śubhakṛtsna devas, the Bṛha devas, and the Parīttabṛha devas.

Having perceived that the Avṛha gods, the Bṛhatphala gods, the Śubhakṛtsna gods, the Anabhraka gods, the Puṇyaprasava gods, the Bṛhat gods, the Atapa gods, the Sudṛśa gods, the Sudarśana gods, and the Akaniṣṭha gods had all assembled and were seated together,
he made them all witnesses and addressed Śakra, the lord of the gods.

Whosoever, Kauśika— be they bodhisattvas mahāsattvas, monks, nuns, laymen, laywomen, sons of noble family, daughters of noble family, or gods and goddesses— who shall take up, bear in mind, master, cultivate, and extensively proclaim this perfection of wisdom to others, [they shall all be protected by me].
They will never be separated from the mind of omniscience (*sarvākārajñatā*). Māra, the Evil One, or the deities belonging to Māra’s host will find no opportunity to gain entry into them.
Why is that?
Because those sons of good family and daughters of good family will have well-established themselves in the very emptiness of form (*rūpaśūnyatā*).
The emptiness of feeling itself will be well-established; the emptiness of perception itself will be well-established; the emptiness of mental formations themselves will be well-established.
Consciousness itself will become well-established in emptiness. For what reason?
Because emptiness does not find an entry into emptiness, nor does the signless find an entry into the signless.
The wishless does not find an entry into the wishless.
For it is because those sons of good family or daughters of good family will have well-established the very emptiness of the eye,
and will have well-established the very emptiness of the ear.
The emptiness of the nose itself will be well-established; the emptiness of the tongue itself will be well-established;
the emptiness of the body itself will be well-established.
The very emptiness of the mind will become well-established. Why is that?
Because emptiness does not find an entry into emptiness, nor does the signless find an entry into the signless.
The wishless does not find an entry into the wishless.
For it is because those sons of good family or daughters of good family will have well-established the very emptiness of form.
The emptiness of sound itself will be well-established;
the emptiness of odor itself will be well-established; the emptiness of taste itself will be well-established.
The emptiness of contact itself will be well-established; the emptiness of phenomena itself will be well-established. Why is that?
Because emptiness does not find an entry point into emptiness.
The signless does not gain entry into the signless,
nor does the wishless gain entry into the wishless.
For it is because those sons of good family or daughters of good family will have firmly established the very emptiness of visual consciousness.
The emptiness of ear-consciousness itself will be well-established;
the emptiness of nose-consciousness itself will be well-established; the emptiness of tongue-consciousness itself will be well-established.
The emptiness of body-consciousness itself will be well-established; the emptiness of mind-consciousness itself will be well-established. Why is that?
Because emptiness does not find an entry point into emptiness.
The signless does not find an entry into the signless,
nor does the wishless find an entry into the wishless.
For it is because those sons of good family or daughters of good family will have well-established themselves in the very emptiness of visual contact.
The emptiness of auditory contact itself will be well-established; the emptiness of olfactory contact itself will be well-established;
the emptiness of gustatory consciousness itself will be well-established.
The emptiness of body-contact itself will be well-established; the emptiness of mind-contact itself will be well-established. Why is that?
Because emptiness does not find an entry point into emptiness.
One does not find an entry into the signless through the signless,
nor does one find an entry into the wishless through the wishless.
This is because those sons of good family or daughters of good family will have firmly established themselves in the very emptiness of feeling conditioned by eye-contact.
The very emptiness of feeling conditioned by auditory contact will be well-established;
the very emptiness of feeling conditioned by olfactory contact will be well-established;
the very emptiness of feeling conditioned by gustatory contact will be well-established.
The emptiness of feeling conditioned by bodily contact will be well-established; the emptiness of feeling conditioned by mental contact will be well-established.
Why is that?
For in this way, emptiness does not find entry into emptiness;
the signless does not find entry into the signless;
and the wishless does not find entry into the wishless.
For in this way, those sons of good family or daughters of good family will have the very emptiness of the earth element well-established;
they will have the very emptiness of the water element well-established; they will have the very emptiness of the fire element well-established.
The emptiness of the wind element itself will be well-established;
the emptiness of the space element itself will be well-established;
the emptiness of the consciousness element itself will be well-established. For what reason?
For thus, emptiness does not find an entry into emptiness,
nor does the signless find an entry into the signless.
The wishless does not find an entry into the wishless.
For it is because those sons of good family or daughters of good family will have well-mastered the very emptiness of ignorance, and will have well-mastered the very emptiness of formative forces.
The emptiness of consciousness itself will be well-established;
the emptiness of name-and-form itself will be well-established; the emptiness of the six sense bases itself will be well-established.
The emptiness of contact itself will be well-established; the emptiness of feeling itself will be well-established;
the emptiness of craving itself will be well-established.
The emptiness of grasping itself will be well-established;
the emptiness of existence itself will be well-established; the emptiness of birth itself will be well-established.
The emptiness of aging and death itself will be well-established.
Why is that?
Because emptiness does not find an entry point into emptiness.
The signless does not gain entry into the signless,
nor does the wishless gain entry into the wishless.
This is because those sons of good family or daughters of good family will have well-sustained the very emptiness of the perfection of giving.
The emptiness of the perfection of ethical discipline itself will be well-sustained; the emptiness of the perfection of patience itself will be well-sustained;
the emptiness of the perfection of vigor itself will be well-sustained.
The very emptiness of the perfection of meditative concentration will be well-sustained; the very emptiness of the perfection of wisdom will be well-sustained.
For what reason?
For in this way, emptiness does not find entry into emptiness;
the signless does not find entry into the signless;
and the wishless does not find entry into the wishless.
For it is because those sons of good family or daughters of good family will have well-established the emptiness of internal emptiness itself,
will have well-established the emptiness of external emptiness itself,
and will have well-established the emptiness of internal-and-external emptiness itself.
The emptiness of emptiness itself will be well-established; the emptiness of great emptiness itself will be well-established;
the emptiness of ultimate emptiness itself will be well-established.
The emptiness of conditioned phenomena will itself be well-established; the emptiness of unconditioned phenomena will itself be well-established;
the emptiness of absolute emptiness will itself be well-established.
The emptiness of the emptiness of that which has no beginning or end will be well-established; the emptiness of the emptiness of non-dispersal will be well-established;
the emptiness of the emptiness of intrinsic nature will be well-established.

The emptiness of the emptiness of all dharmas itself will be well-established; the emptiness of the emptiness of specific characteristics itself will be well-established; the emptiness of the emptiness of non-apprehension itself will be well-established.
The emptiness of the emptiness of non-existence itself will be well-established; the emptiness of the emptiness of intrinsic nature itself will be well-established;
the emptiness of the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence itself will be well-established. For what reason?
For in this way, emptiness does not find an entry into emptiness;
the signless does not find an entry into the signless; and the wishless does not find an entry into the wishless.
For it is thus: those sons of good family or daughters of good family will have the very emptiness of the foundations of mindfulness well-sustained;
they will have the very emptiness of the right efforts well-sustained; they will have the very emptiness of the bases of psychic power well-sustained.
The emptiness of the sense faculties itself will be well-established;
the emptiness of the powers itself will be well-established; the emptiness of the factors of enlightenment itself will be well-established.
The emptiness of the noble eightfold path itself will be well-established.
Why is that?
Because emptiness does not find an entry point into emptiness.
The signless does not find an entry into the signless,
nor does the wishless find an entry into the wishless.
This is because those sons of good family or daughters of good family will have firmly established the very emptiness of the noble truths.

The emptiness of the meditative absorptions (dhyāna) itself will be well-established; the emptiness of the immeasurables (apramāṇa) itself will be well-established; and the emptiness of the formless attainments (ārūpyasamāpatti) itself will be well-established.
The emptiness of the liberations itself will be well-sustained; the emptiness of the successive meditative attainments themselves will be well-sustained;
and the emptiness of the gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—themselves will be well-sustained.
The emptiness of the superknowledges itself will be well-sustained;
the emptiness of meditative concentrations itself will be well-sustained; the emptiness of the gateways of mnemonic formulas itself will be well-sustained. For what reason?
For in this way, emptiness does not find entry into emptiness;
the signless does not find entry into the signless;
and the wishless does not find entry into the wishless.

For it is because those sons of good family or daughters of good family will have themselves empowered by the very emptiness of the powers of a Tathāgata, they will have themselves empowered by the very emptiness of the grounds of self-confidence, and they will have themselves empowered by the very emptiness of the analytical knowledges.
The emptiness of great loving-kindness itself will be well-established; the emptiness of great compassion itself will be well-established;
the emptiness of the unique qualities of a Buddha itself will be well-established. For what reason?
For in this way, emptiness does not find an entry into emptiness;
the signless does not find an entry into the signless;
and the wishless does not find an entry into the wishless.

For it is because those sons of good family or daughters of good family will have themselves empowered by the very emptiness of omniscience (*sarvajñatā-śūnyatā*), will have themselves empowered by the very emptiness of the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā-śūnyatā*),
and will have themselves empowered by the very emptiness of the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā-śūnyatā*). Why is that?
For thus their intrinsic nature does not exist, by which one might find an entry while practicing, nor wherein one might find an entry.

And as for those who might find an opportunity [to harm them], Kausika, no human or non-human being, though seeking an opportunity and looking for an opening, shall find an opportunity against those sons of good family or daughters of good family. Why is that?
Because those sons of good family or daughters of good family [behave] toward all sentient beings...

They have cultivated loving-kindness, compassion, sympathetic joy, and equanimity, and that by way of non-apprehension. Furthermore, that son of good family or daughter of good family shall not meet their end through an untimely death.
Why is that?

Because those sons of good family or daughters of good family, while practicing the perfection of generosity, have attended to all sentient beings with proper care; or rather, Kauśika, [those who have attended to] the three-thousandfold great thousandfold world-system...

The gods of the Four Great Kings, the Trāyastriṃśa gods, the Yāma gods, the Tuṣita gods, the Nirmāṇarati gods, the Paranirmitavaśavartin gods, the Brahmakāyika gods, the Brahmapārṣadya gods, the Brahmapurohita gods,
the Mahābrahmā gods, the Ābhāsvara gods, the Śubhakṛtsna gods, and the Bṛhatphala gods [are dedicated] to the unsurpassed [enlightenment].
Those sons of the gods who have set out for full and perfect enlightenment,
and those sons of the gods by whom this perfection of wisdom has not been heard, nor taken up, nor retained, nor mastered— they should now hear, take up, retain, and master this perfection of wisdom.
They should attend to it thoroughly and must not be separated from the mind of omniscience (*sarvākārajñatā-citta*).

Furthermore, Kauśika, those sons of good family and daughters of good family who will take up, maintain, master, and attend to this perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*) thoroughly shall not be separated from the mind of omniscience.
Furthermore, those sons of good family and daughters of good family who have gone to empty dwellings, or to open spaces, or onto crossroads, will experience neither fear nor paralysis.
Why is that?
Because those sons of good family and daughters of good family have cultivated the forms of internal emptiness through the yoga of non-apprehension.
They have cultivated the external emptinesses through the yoga of non-apprehension; they have cultivated the internal-external emptinesses through the yoga of non-apprehension;
they have cultivated the emptiness of emptiness through the yoga of non-apprehension.
They have cultivated the great emptinesses through the yoga of non-apprehension; they have cultivated the ultimate emptinesses through the yoga of non-apprehension;
they have cultivated the conditioned emptinesses through the yoga of non-apprehension.
They have cultivated the emptiness of the unconditioned through the yoga of non-apprehension;
they have cultivated the ultimate emptiness through the yoga of non-apprehension; they have cultivated the emptiness of that which has no beginning or end through the yoga of non-apprehension.
They have cultivated the emptiness of non-dispersal through the yoga of non-apprehension; they have cultivated the emptiness of intrinsic nature through the yoga of non-apprehension;
they have cultivated the emptiness of all phenomena through the yoga of non-apprehension.

They have cultivated the emptiness of specific characteristics through the yoga of non-apprehension; they have cultivated the emptiness of non-apprehension through the yoga of non-apprehension; they have cultivated the emptiness of non-existence through the yoga of non-apprehension.

They have cultivated the emptiness of intrinsic nature through the yoga of non-apprehension, and they have cultivated the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence through the yoga of non-apprehension.
Then, at that time, as many gods of the Realm of the Four Great Kings as there are in the triple-thousand great thousandfold world system...

The gods of the Thirty-three, the Yāma gods, the Tuṣita gods, the Nirmāṇarati gods, the Paranirmitavaśavartin gods, the Brahmakāyika gods, the Ābhāsvara gods, the Śubhakṛtsna gods, the Bṛhatphala gods, and the Śuddhāvāsakāyika gods— all of them said this to the Blessed One:

"Blessed One, we shall provide constant and continuous protection, shelter, and defense for those sons of good family and daughters of good family who have faith in this profound perfection of wisdom, and who will take it up, bear it in mind, recite it, master it, and attend to it with wise reflection."
And they will proclaim it in detail to others, and they will never be separated from the mental engagement with the knowledge of all aspects. Why is that?
Because, Blessed One, it is by depending upon the bodhisattva mahāsattva that the hells are cut off.
The world of Yama is cut off; the poverty of gods is cut off; the poverty of humans is cut off.

Thus all calamities and misfortunes are cut off and destroyed; the wildernesses of famine do not exist; all are cut off by virtue of the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva. The manifestation of the ten paths of wholesome action occurs in the world.
The manifestation of the four dhyānas occurs in the world;
the manifestation of the four immeasurables occurs in the world;
the manifestation of the four formless attainments occurs in the world.
The manifestation of the five superknowledges occurs in the world;
the manifestation of the perfection of generosity occurs in the world; the manifestation of the perfection of ethical discipline occurs in the world.
The perfection of patience appears in the world; the perfection of vigor appears in the world;
the perfection of meditation appears in the world.
The perfection of wisdom appears in the world.
The emptiness of the internal appears in the world;
the emptiness of the external appears in the world.
The manifestation of internal-external emptiness occurs in the world;
the manifestation of the emptiness of emptiness occurs in the world; the manifestation of great emptiness occurs in the world.
The manifestation of ultimate emptiness occurs in the world;
the manifestation of conditioned emptiness occurs in the world; the manifestation of unconditioned emptiness occurs in the world.
The manifestation of absolute emptiness occurs in the world; the manifestation of the emptiness of that which has no beginning or end occurs in the world;
the manifestation of the emptiness of non-dispersal occurs in the world.
The manifestation of the emptiness of intrinsic nature occurs in the world;
the manifestation of the emptiness of all phenomena occurs in the world;
the manifestation of the emptiness of specific characteristics occurs in the world.
The manifestation of the emptiness of non-apprehension occurs in the world; the manifestation of the emptiness of non-existence occurs in the world;
the manifestation of the emptiness of intrinsic nature occurs in the world.
The emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence appears in the world.
The four foundations of mindfulness appear in the world;
the four right efforts appear in the world.
The manifestation of the four bases of psychic power occurs in the world;
the manifestation of the five faculties occurs in the world;
the manifestation of the five powers occurs in the world.
The appearance of the seven factors of awakening occurs in the world;
the appearance of the noble eightfold path occurs in the world;
the appearance of the four noble truths occurs in the world.
The manifestation of the four dhyānas occurs in the world;
the manifestation of the four immeasurables occurs in the world;
the manifestation of the four formless attainments occurs in the world.
The manifestation of the eight liberations occurs in the world;
the manifestation of the nine successive meditative attainments occurs in the world;
the manifestation of the three gateways to liberation occurs in the world.
The manifestation of the five superknowledges occurs in the world;
the manifestation of all meditative concentrations occurs in the world; the manifestation of all doors of dhāraṇīs occurs in the world.

The manifestation of the ten powers of a Tathāgata occurs in the world; the manifestation of the four grounds of self-confidence occurs in the world; the manifestation of the four analytical knowledges occurs in the world.
The manifestation of great loving-kindness occurs in the world;
the manifestation of great compassion occurs in the world;
and the manifestation of the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha occurs in the world.
The manifestation of omniscience occurs in the world; the manifestation of the knowledge of the aspects of the path occurs in the world;
the manifestation of the knowledge of all aspects occurs in the world.
It is by depending on the bodhisattva mahāsattva that great kṣatriya clans are known, great brahmin clans are known,
and great householder clans are known.
Universal monarchs are known;
the gods of the Four Great Kings are known;
the Trāyastriṃśa gods are known.
The Yāma gods are known;
the Tuṣita gods are known;
the Nirmāṇarati gods are known.
The gods who wield power over the creations of others are known;
the gods of the Brahma-realm are known;
the gods who are ministers of Brahma are known.
The Brahmā-pārṣadya gods are known;
the Mahābrahmā gods are known;
the Ābhāsvara gods are known.
The gods of Limited Radiance are known; the gods of Immeasurable Radiance are known;
the gods of Utmost Radiance are known.
The Śubha gods are known;
the Parīttaśubha gods are known;
the Apramāṇaśubha gods are known.
The Śubhakṛtsna gods are known;
the Bṛhat gods are known;
the Parīttabṛhat gods are known.
The Apramāṇaśubha gods are known;
the Bṛhatphala gods are known;
the Abṛha gods are known. (ŚsP_II-3_230)
The Atapa gods are known; the Sudṛśa gods are known;
the Sudarśana gods are known.
The Akaniṣṭha gods are known;
it is by depending on the bodhisattva mahāsattva that the fruit of stream-entry is known,
and the stream-enterer is known.
The fruit of once-returning is discerned,
the once-returner is discerned,
and the fruit of non-returning is discerned.
The non-returner is known,
arhatship is known, and the arhat is known.
Pratyekabodhi is made known,
the Pratyekabuddha is made known,
and it is by depending upon the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva that the ripening of sentient beings is made known.
The purification of the buddha-field is made known;
the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas are made known in the world; and the turning of the wheel of Dharma is made known.
The jewel of the Buddha is known, the jewel of the Dharma is known,
and the jewel of the Saṅgha is known.
"And by this method, Blessed One, protection, shelter, and guardianship should be provided for a bodhisattva mahāsattva by the world with its gods, humans, and asuras.
When this had been said, the Blessed One spoke thus to Śakra, the lord of the gods:
"So it is, Kauśika, so it is."
Depending upon the bodhisattva mahāsattva, there occurs the manifestation in the world of the ten paths of wholesome action;
there occurs the manifestation in the world of the four dhyānas;
and there occurs the manifestation in the world of the four immeasurables.
The manifestation of the four formless attainments occurs in the world;
the manifestation of the five supernormal powers occurs in the world;
the manifestation of the perfection of generosity occurs in the world.
The perfection of ethical discipline appears in the world; the perfection of patience appears in the world;
the perfection of vigor appears in the world.
The perfection of meditation appears in the world; the perfection of wisdom appears in the world.
The emptiness of the internal appears in the world.
The manifestation of external emptiness occurs in the world;
the manifestation of internal-external emptiness occurs in the world;
the manifestation of the emptiness of emptiness occurs in the world.
The appearance of great emptiness occurs in the world; the appearance of ultimate emptiness occurs in the world;
the appearance of conditioned emptiness occurs in the world.
The manifestation of the emptiness of the unconditioned occurs in the world;
the manifestation of absolute emptiness occurs in the world; the manifestation of the emptiness of that which has no beginning or end occurs in the world.
The emptiness of non-dispersal appears in the world; the emptiness of intrinsic nature appears in the world;
the emptiness of all phenomena appears in the world.
The emptiness of specific characteristics appears in the world;
the emptiness of non-apprehension appears in the world; the emptiness of non-existence appears in the world.
The emptiness of intrinsic nature appears in the world; the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence appears in the world.
The manifestation of the four foundations of mindfulness occurs in the world;
the manifestation of the four right efforts occurs in the world;
the manifestation of the four bases of psychic power occurs in the world.
The manifestation of the five faculties occurs in the world;
the manifestation of the five powers occurs in the world; the manifestation of the seven factors of awakening occurs in the world.
The appearance of the noble eightfold path occurs in the world;
the appearance of the four noble truths occurs in the world;
the appearance of the four meditative absorptions occurs in the world.
There is the manifestation in the world of the four immeasurables;
there is the manifestation in the world of the four formless attainments;
there is the manifestation in the world of the eight liberations.
The manifestation of the nine successive meditative attainments occurs in the world;
the manifestation of the three gateways to liberation occurs in the world;
the manifestation of the five superknowledges occurs in the world.
The manifestation of all samādhis occurs in the world; the manifestation of all dhāraṇī-gates occurs in the world;
the manifestation of the ten powers of a Tathāgata occurs in the world.
The manifestation of the four grounds of self-confidence occurs in the world;
the manifestation of the four analytical knowledges occurs in the world;
the manifestation of great loving-kindness occurs in the world.
The manifestation of great compassion occurs in the world;
the manifestation of the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha occurs in the world;
the manifestation of omniscience occurs in the world.
The knowledge of the aspects of the path appears in the world;
the knowledge of all aspects appears in the world.
It is by depending upon the bodhisattva mahāsattva that the great kshatriya clans are known.
Families of great brahmins are known; families of great householders are known;
universal monarch kings are known.
The gods of the Four Great Kings are known;
the Trāyastriṃśa gods are known;
the Yāma gods are known.
The Tuṣita gods are known;
the Nirmāṇarati gods are known; the Paranirmitavaśavartin gods are known.
The gods of the Brahma-realm are known;
the gods who are ministers of Brahma are known;
the gods who are the retinue of Brahma are known.
The Mahābrahmā gods are known;
the Ābhāsvara gods are known;
the Parītābha gods are known.
The gods of Immeasurable Light are known; the gods of Radiant Purity are known;
the gods of Purity are known.
The Parītaśubha gods are known; the Apramāṇaśubha gods are known;
the Śubhakṛtsna gods are known.
The Bṛha gods are known;
the Parītabṛha gods are known;
the Apramāṇabṛha gods are known.
The Bṛhatphala gods are known;
the Abṛha gods are known.
The Atapa gods are known; the Sudṛśa gods are known;
the Sudarśana gods are known.
The Akaniṣṭha gods are known.
It is by depending upon the bodhisattva mahāsattva that the fruit of stream-entry is known,
and the stream-enterer is known.
The fruit of once-returning is discerned,
the once-returner is discerned,
and the fruit of non-returning is discerned.
The non-returner is known,
arhatship is known, and the arhat is known.
Pratyekabodhi is discerned;
the pratyekabuddha is discerned.
It is by depending upon the bodhisattva mahāsattva that the ripening of sentient beings is discerned.
The purification of the buddha-field is made known;
the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas are made known in the world; and the turning of the wheel of Dharma is made known.
The jewel of the Buddha is recognized, the jewel of the Dharma is recognized,
and the jewel of the Saṅgha is recognized.
Therefore, Bodhisattvas, Mahāsattvas, should be honored, revered, esteemed, and worshiped by the world with its gods, humans, and asuras;
and protection, shelter, and defense should be constantly and continuously provided for them.
For, Kauśika, one who honors, reveres, esteems, and values this [teaching] honors, reveres, esteems, and values me.
One should regard the bodhisattva mahāsattva as one who is to be honored, revered, esteemed, and worshipped.

Therefore, the bodhisattva mahāsattva should be honored, revered, esteemed, and worshipped by the world with its gods, humans, and asuras; and there should be constant and continuous protection, defense, and guardianship for him.
And furthermore, Kauśika, this great trichiliocosm...
Suppose a world-system were completely filled with disciples and pratyekabuddhas, just like a thicket of reeds, or a thicket of sugarcane,

or a thicket of *śara* grass, or a thicket of *śāra* grass, or a thicket of *śāri* grass, or a thicket of sesame; and suppose some son of good family or daughter of good family were to honor, respect, and worship them for as long as life lasts with all kinds of requisites.

and were to honor, revere, respect, and worship a single bodhisattva mahāsattva who has first produced the thought of awakening and is not separated from the six perfections— this latter person would generate far more merit than that. Why is that?
Furthermore, Kauśika, it is not by depending on those śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas that a bodhisattva mahāsattva is known in the world,
nor is a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha known in the world.
Rather, Kauśika, it is by depending on the bodhisattva mahāsattva that all śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas are known in the world.

The Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas are known in the world. Therefore, Kauśika, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva should be honored, revered, esteemed, and worshipped by the world including its gods, humans, and asuras;
and protection, defense, and guardianship should be constantly and continuously provided for him.
